title: fix(plasma): Plasma Profile takes a start pick and an exit pick
body:
## What changed

- Plasma Profile takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `Ring` (`KindInfo::pick()`).
- The picks are the operation-level `picks` of #3339 / PR #3871. This PR adds no field, no command and no MCP tool.
- Start pick: the lead-in of the nearest closed contour lands on the projection of the pick on the profile. The pierce is at the start of that lead-in, in the scrap.
- Exit pick: the torch cuts the full contour. Then it cuts on to the projection of the exit pick. The lead-out leaves there and the torch goes off at its end.
- Small-hole rule: the pierce stays at the centre and there is no lead-out. A start pick sets where the straight lead-in meets the hole. An exit pick sets where the torch goes off. It must be at or past the overburn.
- Each contour without a pick keeps its automatic seam.
- A pick that a law cannot hold is refused by name. It is never moved. The text names the role and the point:
  - a pick farther than 1.5 kerf widths from each closed profile;
  - a pick when the operation has open runs only;
  - a lead-in or a lead-out with no room beside the part at the pick (the pierce or the torch off would be on the part);
  - a small-hole lead-in from the centre that would cross the part;
  - a small-hole exit pick inside the overburn;
  - an exit pick with control compensation (G41/G42), at the command door and in the generator.
- The kerf law and the cover law still judge the complete path.
- New generator door: `camcraft_motion::plasma::plasma_profile_picked`. `plasma_profile` calls it with no pick.

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for Plasma Profile. The command refused each pick on the kind. The generator always chose the seam (`longest_mid`, or the point nearest the centre for a small hole).

## Where the issue is silent (smallest change taken)

- Which contour takes a pick: the closed contour whose profile is nearest. The reach is 1.5 kerf widths (the 2D contour uses 1.5 tool diameters).
- How the cut gets to the exit: a run past the start in the cut direction. The stretch between the start and the exit is cut two times. A note on the path gives its length.
- "After the overburn": only the small-hole rule has an overburn. There the exit must be at or past it. A contour with leads has no overburn, so the exit pick alone sets the run.
- An exit pick with G41/G42 is refused by name. The programmed contour ends at its start, and a longer one needs a new proof of the compensation span. Mutation M2 showed that the generator emits a path without that refusal.
- Waterjet: `WaterjetProfile` is on `main` now, with its own planner and tabs. This PR does not change it. A pick on it is still refused by name. The slice is #3983.
- UI: this PR changes no UI file. The operation page reads `KindInfo::pick()`.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/3334-plasma-start-exit.md`.

## Tests

Final head: `845228ac0`, on `upstream/main` `10ea81a2a`.

Pins (new):

- `camcraft-app`, `start_exit_shared` suite, submodule `start_exit_shared/plasma.rs` (7 tests):
  - `the_pierce_is_at_the_start_pick_and_the_torch_goes_off_at_the_exit_pick` (golden CL `plasma_start_exit_picks.cl`)
  - `a_pick_whose_pierce_falls_on_the_part_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pick_that_is_far_from_each_profile_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_small_hole_keeps_its_rule_under_the_picks`
  - `an_exit_pick_under_control_compensation_is_refused_at_the_door`
  - `undo_and_redo_restore_the_picks_and_the_path`
  - `the_plasma_profile_takes_a_start_pick_and_an_exit_pick`
- `camcraft-app`, `mcp_plasma`: `plasma_mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_start_and_exit_picks` (MCP `edit_operation` sets the picks, `generate` holds them, undo clears them, a far pick is refused by name).
- `camcraft-app`, `start_exit_shared`: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (extended: Plasma Profile is `Ring`).
- `camcraft-motion` lib, `plasma::picks_tests` (9 tests), with `no_pick_is_the_automatic_path_move_for_move`.

Red before the fix: I put the six source files of `upstream/main` back and ran the app pins. All 7 plasma pick tests failed, the MCP pin failed and the capability test failed (`left: NotTaken("the planner chooses the entry and the exit of this kind until its slice of #1448 ships")`). With the fix, all pass.

Mutation results (one guard off for each run, then restored; each run was red, and green after the restore):

| # | Guard off | Red test |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | reach (`d > reach`) | `plasma::picks_tests::a_pick_that_no_law_can_hold_is_refused_by_name` |
| M2 | exit pick with control compensation (generator) | `plasma::picks_tests::control_compensation_holds_the_start_pick_and_refuses_the_exit_pick` |
| M3 | open runs take no pick | `plasma::picks_tests::a_pick_that_no_law_can_hold_is_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | `PathPicks::refusal` (two picks of a role, a pick that is not a number) | `plasma::picks_tests::a_pick_that_no_law_can_hold_is_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | small-hole lead-in across the part | `plasma::picks_tests::a_small_hole_lead_in_that_would_cross_the_part_is_refused_by_name` (the kerf law still refused the path, without the name of the pick) |
| M6 | small-hole exit inside the overburn | `plasma::picks_tests::a_small_hole_keeps_its_rule_and_its_overburn` |
| M7 | the name of the pick in the lead refusal | `a_pick_whose_pierce_falls_on_the_part_is_refused_by_name` |

I moved the pin file into the `start_exit_shared` suite. The source files did not change after the full run.

All passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the final head.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: not completed. Step `[01] light build (release --no-run)` did not get past three dependency crates (`boa_engine`, `flecs_ecs`, `reqwest`) in 50 minutes on the shared machine. I stopped it. No light step ran, so there is no light result for this head. The light twins are `motion light: lib`, three `adaptive_troch_*` suites and `app light: pocket_pass_start`. The review must run this lane.

## Goldens moved

- Added: `crates/app/tests/golden/plasma_start_exit_picks.cl` (new file, the picked path of the pin).
- Changed: none. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" examples/catalog` shows only the new file. `golden_cl` (with `plasma_plate_with_holes.cl`) and the three `example_catalog*` suites pass without a regeneration.

- The full heavy lanes. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 107 release steps. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) gives a `P2` PR no heavy step, and the full lanes run at the cut. No heavy test in the reach is a plasma test.
- The posted G-code of a picked path on a machine. `plasma_post` and `post_serves_plasma` pass, but no new posted golden has a pick. The CL golden pins the path.
- The GUI. No UI file changed, so there is no screenshot. I did not start the application.
- The waterjet kind (#3983).
- A pick on a part with many nested contours at almost the same distance from the pick.

## Overlaps

- #3980, #3978, #3970, #3981: they touch `KindInfo::pick()` in `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs` and the kind list in `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared.rs`. Each changes the arm of its own kind. Whichever merges second refreshes.

title: fix(turning): Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish take a start and an exit pick
body:
Slice 1 of #3331: Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish. This PR does not close the issue. The eight other turning kinds are the next slices.

## What changed

- A turning pick is a point in the lathe (Z, X) plane. It is a model point `[x, y, z]`. The planner reads it as (station, radius) about the fitted turning axis.
- Start: one rapid goes from the opening point of the path to the pick. The first feed starts at the pick and ends where it ended before.
- Exit: one feed goes from the end of the last feed to the pick. One rapid goes from the pick to the old end point of the path.
- The moves between the first feed and the last feed do not change.
- New module `crates/motion/src/turning/start_exit.rs` (`with_picks`, `PickLaw`). It works on the finished path of a kernel. The kernels do not change.
- The registry has a new capability, `PickCapability::Meridian`, for the three kinds.
- Threading says "not taken" with its own reason: "the thread start law sets the start and the exit of a thread". The G76 start judge does not change.
- MCP: the `edit_operation` schema names the three kinds and says that z is necessary. `list_operation_types` gives `start_exit.plane` for them.
- UI: the Geometry tab of the three kinds has a Start point group and an Exit point group. The rows are typed (Z and X). Apply uses `EditOperationParams`.

A pick is refused by name, and is never moved, when one of these is true:

- The pick has no Z (refused at the command door, with the name of the kind).
- The pick is not in air: it is inside the stock radius and behind the free end, each grown by the nose radius.
- The pick is on the chuck side of the bar.
- The rapid to the start, or the rapid from the exit, crosses the stock envelope.
- The feed between the pick and the cut comes nearer to the part than nose radius + stock to leave - tolerance.
- The exit feed runs along the surface that the last pass cut.
- The path has canned cycles or control compensation.

## Cause

The turning kinds had the `picks` field of #3339, but no planner read it. The registry gave each turning kind the "owed" reason, so the command door refused each pick.

## Where the issue is silent

- The issue does not say how the tool gets from the pick to the first pass. I chose the smallest change: the first feed of the kernel starts at the pick. The kernel ladder does not change.
- The issue does not say which stock a rapid must miss. I chose the envelope of the part and the setup stock. It does not follow stock that earlier operations removed. This is the safe side.
- The issue does not ask for a viewport pick. A turning point is in air, so the wall snap of the 2D Contour pick is not correct for it. The rows are typed.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/3331-turning-start-exit.md`.

## Tests

Pins (all on the final head `255413391`):

- `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared/turning.rs` (8 tests, in the existing `start_exit_shared` binary):
  - `the_first_pass_starts_at_the_start_pick`
  - `the_last_pass_leaves_at_the_exit_pick`
  - `a_start_and_an_exit_pick_hold_together`
  - `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pick_whose_move_crosses_the_part_or_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`
  - `threading_keeps_its_start_law_and_says_so_by_name`
  - `undo_and_redo_restore_the_path`
  - `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_turning_picks_and_undo_clears_them`
- `crates/motion/src/turning/start_exit_tests.rs` (8 unit tests, `turning::start_exit::tests::*`).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turning_start_exit_tests.rs` (4 tests, `egui_app::turning_start_exit_rows::tests::*`).
- `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` now includes the new capability (an expected change of a pinned list).

Pin proof (the guard was removed, the pin was run, the guard was put back):

| Guard removed | Result | Red test |
|---|---|---|
| `generate.rs` of `upstream/main` (no pick laid) | red | 6 of the 8 app tests: `the_first_pass_starts_at_the_start_pick`, `the_last_pass_leaves_at_the_exit_pick`, `a_start_and_an_exit_pick_hold_together`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name`, `a_pick_whose_move_crosses_the_part_or_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`, `undo_and_redo_restore_the_path` |
| the "needs a Z" door in `pick_kinds.rs` | red | `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_turning_picks_and_undo_clears_them` |
| the Threading reason | red | `threading_keeps_its_start_law_and_says_so_by_name` |
| the early return for no pick | red | `no_pick_gives_the_path_back_unchanged` |

| start rapid crosses the stock | red | `a_rapid_through_the_bar_is_refused_by_name` |

- `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` (in the quick gate);
- `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_inch`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `golden_cl`;
- the turning suites of the quick gate (`turning`, `turning_profile`, `turning_face_approach`, `turning_face_seed` and the others).

`with_picks` returns the path before it reads a number when there is no pick. `no_pick_gives_the_path_back_unchanged` pins this.

title: fix(sinker): Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn take a start and an exit pick
body:
## What changed

- The Sinker Burn takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `PickCapability::Ring`: the ring is its orbit.
  - A pick is an angle round the burn position (`x`, `y`). The start pick is where the orbit starts. The exit pick is where the orbit ends.
  - Circular: the circle starts at the start angle and makes one full turn counter-clockwise. With an exit pick it continues to the exit angle.
  - Planetary: the spiral turns from the start angle and reaches the radius there. The closing circle starts there.
  - Vector: the vector toward the start pick is burned first. The vector toward the exit pick is burned last.
  - After the exit angle the electrode feeds back to the burn position and retracts up the burn axis, as before.
- The Sinker Side Burn takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `PickCapability::Ends`.
  - The side move has two ends: the burn position and the wall end (the burn position moved by `amount` toward the wall).
  - A pick on the wall side of the middle of the move chooses the wall end. A pick on the other side chooses the burn position.
  - The start pick chooses the end where the electrode plunges. The exit pick chooses the end where it retracts.
- These picks are refused by name, at the command door and at generation. No pick is moved.
  - A pick on a Sinker Burn without an orbit: `Sinker Burn: a start point is not taken without an orbit - a straight plunge starts and ends at the burn position; ...`.
  - A pick on the burn position: it gives the orbit no angle.
  - A pick between two vectors of a vector orbit: `... is on no vector of the orbit ...`.
  - An exit vector that the vector order cannot end on.
  - A side burn pick at the middle of the side move: it chooses no end.
- With no pick each generator calls the earlier function. Each path without a pick is byte-identical.
- A path with a pick has one more note. The note names the start point and the exit point.
- The Geometry tab of each kind has a "Start point" group and an "Exit point" group with typed X and Y rows. A Sinker Burn without an orbit shows "Not taken - a straight plunge starts and ends at the burn position; state an orbit on the Passes tab".
- The schema text of MCP `edit_operation` names the two kinds. `list_operation_types` answers `start_exit: { start: true, exit: true, field: "picks" }` for them.

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn. The door refused each pick. `sinker_orbit::orbit_offsets` always started the orbit at +X. `sinker_side::side_burn_worn` always plunged and retracted at the burn position.

## Design

The issue is exact about what each pick sets. Where it is silent, I took the smallest change. The decision file is `docs/decisions/3333-sinker-start-exit.md`.

- **The laws hold at each angle.** A circle keeps its own vertices, and the start and the exit are added vertices. The four axis directions stay vertices, so the walls move out by exactly the radius. Each vertex is on or inside the radius (`sinker_orbit::on_disc`). The undersize law and the cavity limits (`cavity_x`, `cavity_y`) count the radius, so they hold. A vector orbit keeps its directions; a pick changes the order only.
- **The orbit returns to the burn position before the retract.** The layered burn plunges each layer on the burn axis, so the orbit must end there between two layers. The retract law is not changed. The issue says "where the orbit ends before the retract": the last position on the radius is the exit angle.
- **The side burn's ends.** The issue says "the side where the side move begins". I read "side" as an end of the move. The `direction` parameter stays the one input for the wall. The electrode is at the same two positions at the same tip for each choice, so the burned volume is the same. `side_burn_worn` runs first, so the allowance law, the wear law and the layer law refuse before a pick is read.
- **No new field.** The picked generators take the ends as an argument: `sinker_wear::burn_compensated_between` and `sinker_picks::side_burn_between`. `SinkerParams` and `Orbit` are not changed.
- **No new command and no new file key.** The picks use the existing `EditOperationParams` and the `picks` field of #3339. The stamp already includes the picks.
- The new code is in one motion module, `crates/motion/src/sinker_picks.rs`. The UI rows are in one new file, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/sinker_pick_rows.rs`.

## Tests

Pins in the `start_exit_shared` suite of `camcraft-app` (`crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared/sinker.rs` and `sinker_side.rs`). Each name below has the prefix `sinker::`. The first seven were red before the fix, on unchanged `upstream/main` code at `707dac12a`. No new test binary is added.

- `a_planetary_orbit_reaches_its_radius_at_the_start_pick`
- `a_vector_orbit_starts_on_the_picked_vector_and_ends_on_the_exit_vector`
- `a_pick_that_the_orbit_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`
- `side::a_side_burn_starts_and_ends_at_the_picked_ends_of_its_side_move` (five choices of ends; the wall position in the stock sim; no gouge; undo and redo restore the previous path)
- `side::a_side_burn_pick_at_the_middle_of_the_move_is_refused_by_name`
- `side::mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_sinker_picks_and_refuses_an_impossible_one_by_name`
- `side::the_generator_refuses_an_impossible_sinker_pick_by_name` (added with the fix; it calls `operation::generate` directly)
- `a_picked_orbit_keeps_the_undersize_law_and_the_cavity_limits` (added with the fix; a rough pass with a pick generates inside the radius, and an orbit past the cavity is refused by the undersize law)

More tests:

title: fix(slot): a Slot takes a start point and an exit point
body:
First slice of #3325: the Slot kind. The other kinds of the table stay refused by name.

## What changed

- A Slot takes a start point and an exit point (`PickCapability::Ends`).
- A start pick chooses the slot end where the pass starts. The cutter goes down at that end.
- An exit pick chooses the slot end where the pass stops.
- New planner `machining2d::slot_picked_ends` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_picks.rs`). It returns `(a, b)` or `(b, a)`. It does nothing else.
- The Slot arm of `generate.rs` calls the planner after `slot_extended_ends`, then calls `slot` as before.
- The Slot's Lead in / Lead out tab draws the Start point and Exit point groups. The viewport pick and the viewport marks take the Slot.
- MCP: `edit_operation` sets `picks` on a Slot (the field of #3339). `list_operation_types` answers `start: true, exit: true` for the Slot.

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for the Slot, so `sane.rs` refused each pick. The slot planner did not read a pick.

## Design (where the issue is silent, the smallest change)

- A pick only swaps the two ends. `slot(b, a)` is `slot(a, b)` turned half a turn about the middle of the slot. A half turn keeps the stadium, the rows, the wall lap and the climb sense. No new move shape is made. The test `a_swap_is_the_same_pass_turned_half_a_turn` proves this move by move, arcs included.
- Without a pick the planner returns its input. Each earlier slot is the same to the byte.
- Exit: the row count decides where a pass stops. An odd count stops at the end opposite the start. An even count stops at the end where it started (the wall lap of #2906 closes there). The issue says "the other end" for the exit. That holds for an odd count. For an even count the exit is at the start end, and a pick at the other end is refused by name.
- A start pick and an exit pick together: the start decides. An exit pick at the end where the pass does not stop is refused by name. The refusal gives the two ends and the row count.
- An exit pick alone turns the pass so that it stops at the nearest end.
- Reach: a pick farther from the cutter path than `1.5 x tool diameter + stock to leave` is refused by name. This is the contour's law (`contour_start.rs` `reach`). The cutter path is the stadium of the rows. A pick beside the middle of a long slot is in reach and takes the nearest end.
- A pick the same distance from both ends is refused by name. It names no end.
- A tilted (3+2) slot refuses a pick by name, as the tilted contour does. A pick is a model-frame point.
- The end extensions keep their ends: `extend_start` stays on `a`, `extend_end` on `b`. The #1504 room judges the authored slot as before.
- Entry law, first traverse and the keep-stock check judge the result as before. The start end already changed with the climb flag, so a start at either end is a pass that the generator made before this change.
- `docs/decisions/3325-slot-start-exit.md` has the full record.

## Tests

New test binary reasons:

- `crates/motion/tests/slot_start_exit.rs` groups the Slot end-selection and row-parity laws; no Slot directory suite exists.
- `crates/app/tests/slot_start_exit.rs` groups the Slot command, project-file, MCP, and generation checks; no Slot directory suite exists.

Pins:

- `crates/motion/tests/slot_start_exit.rs` (7 tests, new): `no_pick_is_the_earlier_slot`, `a_swap_is_the_same_pass_turned_half_a_turn`, `the_entry_is_at_the_end_nearest_the_start_pick`, `the_exit_is_at_the_end_nearest_the_exit_pick`, `both_picks_hold_or_the_exit_is_refused_by_name`, `a_pick_that_names_no_end_is_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_that_cannot_be_cut_keeps_its_own_refusal_under_a_pick`. They run one row, three rows and two rows, each with climb and with conventional.
- `crates/app/tests/slot_start_exit.rs` (6 tests, new): capability, entry at the pick, exit at the pick, refusals by name (impossible exit, out of reach, the middle, a tilted slot), command + undo + redo + project file + stamp, MCP `edit_operation` and `list_operation_types`.
- `crates/ui`: `the_slot_lead_tab_has_both_point_groups_and_takes_a_start` (page, Apply, undo) and `a_slot_takes_the_viewport_pick_and_shows_its_marks`.
- `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared.rs`: the capability list now expects `Ends` for the Slot (an expected change).

Red before the fix: the 6 app tests failed on unchanged `upstream/main` (`ddee3aed6`). Each failed with "Slot: a start point is not taken ..." or with `NotTaken` in place of `Ends`.

| Mutation | Result |

The Slot page, Lead in / Lead out tab (rendered from the real page code with `egui_kittest`):

| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1eb1d0af49feee812dddf558e48d5905af2f700b/pr-3978/slot-leads-before-off.png) | ![after off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1eb1d0af49feee812dddf558e48d5905af2f700b/pr-3978/slot-leads-after-off.png) | ![after start set](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1eb1d0af49feee812dddf558e48d5905af2f700b/pr-3978/slot-leads-after-start-set.png) |

The images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch only. The third image shows the gap that "Not exercised" describes.

## Not exercised

- No run on a machine. No simulation of a picked slot against a part model: the swap gives a pass that the generator already made for the other climb sense, and the gouge laws judge it as before.
- Helix and ramp entries with a pick have no pin of their own. The entry certificate is the same stadium for both end orders (the half turn law).
- The Trochoidal Slot, Pocket, 2D Offset, Circular, Trace, Engrave and 2D Chamfer take no pick yet. Each is a later slice of #3325.
- The sentence in the `edit_operation` schema that lists the kinds is not changed. PR #3957 changes the next line, and an edit there makes a merge conflict. `list_operation_types` is the stated source and it names the Slot.

The rows below it (the consequence line and the Exit point group) are then below the page. The 2D Contour page on `upstream/main` shows the same in the same harness, so this is not from this PR. The verifier shares model sections for geometric queries inside prismatic Z slabs of a ramped path.
A flat cut plane keeps its own section. A sloped wall keeps the plane-by-plane reading.

Law (b) asks the distance test before `edge_is_wall`.

title: fix(ui): the tool window's next tool number skips reserved pockets; the full-probe refusal says what to do
body:
## What changed

Three items from the delta safety read of PR #3284 (#2604):

1. **The tool window's next number.** When you add a tool, the window compares the typed number with the number `AddTool` will give, and queues `SetToolNumber` only when they differ. The window used `tool_numbers::next_free`, which ignores the machine's reserved pockets. With T1 reserved for a probe, a typed 1 queued nothing, and the cutter became T2 with no message. A new function, `tool_numbers::next_free_for`, calls the same allocation as `AddTool` (`tool_reservations::allocate`), and the window uses it. Now a typed 1 goes to `SetToolNumber`, which refuses it by name.
2. **Every probe pocket is full.** A new probe is still refused (a probe in an ordinary pocket can break the control's probe macros). The refusal now names the pockets and says what to do:
   `tool 'Probe 2': the probe pockets of <model> (T1) all hold a tool. Delete or renumber the tool in one of these pockets, or reserve one more probe pocket in the machine file`
3. **Plain words.** A refusal names a `tool_setter` reservation as "tool setter", in the app and in the post check of the tool stream. The word "probe" does not change, so the tests and agents that match on it still match.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/3667-tool-reservations.md`.

## How tested

- New app tests in `crates/app/tests/tool_reservations.rs`: `next_free_for_a_new_tool_matches_add_tool`, `a_probe_with_every_probe_pocket_full_says_what_to_do`, `a_tool_setter_pocket_is_named_in_plain_words`.
- New UI test `egui_app::tool_number_tests::a_new_tools_typed_number_is_compared_with_the_reserved_aware_allocation`. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- `cargo xtask gate quick`: 29 of 29 steps pass.

## Not exercised

The Add tool button in the desktop app was not clicked. The UI test calls the same function that the button calls.

title: fix(mcp): a pre-hello client cannot hold the ui link session
body:
## What changed

The UI link served one client at a time, and the token check only ran
when a complete line arrived. A local client without the token could
connect, send no newline, and hold the only session for the 5-minute
`IDLE_TIMEOUT`, blocking `camcraft-cli --ui`, while the app buffered up
to 16 MiB (`MAX_LINE`) for it.

Two new named constants in `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`:

- `PRE_HELLO_DEADLINE`: 5 s. A client that has not sent its hello line
  within 5 s of connecting is closed. The server writes its warning
  note ("no hello line in Ns") before the drop.
- `PRE_HELLO_MAX_LINE`: 4 KiB. The buffered-bytes cap before the token
  check; the drop message stays the existing "message too long" line.

In `serve_client`, the effective idle window is `idle.min(PRE_HELLO_DEADLINE)`
while the gate (the token) is still set, and the room computation and the
post-read cap check use the pre-hello cap until then. After the hello
passes, the 5-minute `IDLE_TIMEOUT` and the 16 MiB `MAX_LINE` apply as
before. No behaviour changes for `Inbox::listen` (no token, gate never
set) or for the in-process channel.

The busy test's client 1 in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` used
to simulate a slow call by connecting and staying silent - under the fix
that client is dropped after 5 s, so it now sends a real hello line and
holds the session like a served call. Its asserted behaviour (a second
call exits 4, busy) is unchanged.

## The pin

`a_client_that_sends_no_hello_cannot_hold_the_session`
(`crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs`): client 1 connects and sends
nothing. Client 2, with the token, retries `link_call` (the link gives
up exit 4 while the session is held) and is served within seconds - the
whole test finishes in about 5.6 s. Without the pre-hello deadline the
silent client holds the session for 5 minutes, the retry bound expires,
and the test fails.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live ui_link`: 7 passed, 0 failed (5.3 s)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 307 passed, 0 failed (36.8 s)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

## What was not exercised

- The Unix-socket transport path of the link (tests run on Windows TCP;
  the unix arms compile but were not run here).
- A client that trickles hello bytes past 4 KiB without a newline is
  covered by the same cap check, but only the no-hello path is pinned
  by a test.
- No real `camcraft-cli` binary run against a silent holder beyond what
  the existing busy test does.

Changelog: `camcraft-cli --ui` is no longer blockable for 5 minutes by a
local process that opens the link port and sends nothing.

Fixes #3873

title: fix(mcp): the cli talks only to the window that proves the token
body:
﻿## What changed

Sibling of #3873 (the server side, PR pending). On Windows a crashed window leaves its discovery file `<pid>.json`, and the CLI opened a session with any peer on that stale port that answered `HELLO_OK` - the peer never proved that it knew the token. This PR closes the client side, all three closes from the issue:

- **The token proof.** The CLI sends a fresh nonce in its hello (`camcraft_link`/`token`/`nonce`). The window answers `HELLO_OK` extended with a `proof`: two FNV-1a 64-bit words (the published public-domain parameters) over `token`, a zero byte, `nonce`. No new crypto dependency - the token itself already crosses the same socket in the clear, so the proof only binds the answer to a peer that read the discovery file and saw this client's fresh nonce. The client refuses a peer whose answer does not prove it. A hello without a nonce (an older CLI) still gets the plain `HELLO_OK` answer, so old CLIs keep working against a new window.
- **The pid-alive check.** Before it connects, the CLI checks that the pid in each entry is alive (`kill(pid, 0)` on Unix, `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)` + `GetExitCodeProcess` on Windows) and removes the file of a dead pid - never a live window's file. When the check cannot say (an access error), the entry stays and the token proof guards the connection. `libc` (unix) and `windows-sys` (Windows) joined as target deps; both are already in the lock through other deps - no new crate.
- **The size and deadline limits.** One answer line is bounded at 1 MiB (`MAX_ANSWER`), a `--ui mcp` bridge session at 256 MiB (`MAX_BRIDGE`); the `HELLO_TIMEOUT` deadline (5 s) covers the whole proof exchange. After the proof, no read deadline applies on purpose: a tool may run for minutes (#3751), and the peer has then proved that it read the discovery file, so the bound on what it may send is the remaining check.

## The pin

`crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs`:

- `a_false_window_that_does_not_prove_the_token_gets_no_tool_call`: a false server on the port of a discovery entry (it has the token, a live pid) answers a plain `HELLO_OK` with no proof. The CLI exits 1, and the only line the false server received is the hello with the nonce - no `tools/call`.
- `a_cli_call_with_no_window_says_so_and_exits_3` now also pins that the CLI removes the file of a dead pid, and does not remove a live pid's file.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live ui_link`: 7 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 307 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No test drives `--ui mcp` (`bridge`) against a peer that overruns `MAX_BRIDGE`; the bound is the same take-based read as the call path.
- The refusal of a recorded (replayed) proof answer is covered by the nonce design, not by a test.
- Only expected overlap with #3873: both-added tests in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs`.

Changelog: the CLI UI link now talks only to a window that proves the link token, and removes the stale link file of a dead pid (Windows local-user hardening, #3874)

title: fix(drilling): Drill, Bore and Thread take a start and an exit pick as the hole order
body:
## What changed

- Drill, Bore and Thread (mill) take a start pick and an exit pick. Their pick capability is `PickCapability::HoleOrder`.
- The hole under the start pick is cut first. The hole under the exit pick is cut last.
- The holes between keep the list order, rotated to the start hole. Example, list A B C D: start C gives C D A B. Exit B gives A C D B. Start C with exit D gives C A B D.
- A pick is on a hole when it is inside the circle of the hole. The nearer centre wins when two circles hold the pick.
- With no pick, the hole list is not changed. Each program without a pick is byte-identical.
- These picks are refused by name. No pick is moved to a different hole.
  - A pick that is on no hole: `Drill: the start point (40.000, 30.000) is not on a hole of this operation - ...`.
  - A start pick and an exit pick on the same hole, when the list has more than one hole.
  - A pick on a Drill with cross holes.
  - A pick on a lathe's axial Drill (refused in the generator, because it needs the machine).
- The operation page of the three kinds has typed rows: "First hole stated", "First hole X / Y", "Last hole stated", "Last hole X / Y". A group that is switched on seeds the first (or the last) hole of the list.
- The schema text of MCP `edit_operation` names the three kinds. `list_operation_types` answers `start_exit: { start: true, exit: true, field: "picks" }` for them.
- Probe is not changed. Its row says "Not taken - a probe touches the part and cuts no path".

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for Drill, Bore and Thread. The door refused each pick. The three arms of `generate` gave the hole list to the kernel in the list order (`drilling::drill`, `machining2d::bore_started`, `machining2d::thread_mill`). A direct `operation::generate` call ignored the picks without a note.

## Design

The issue and #3324 name the capability, the refusals and the example rule "the list order, rotated to the start". Where they are silent, I took the smallest change:

- "Near a hole" is "inside the circle of the hole". A search distance is not used.
- The rule is one function, `camcraft_motion::drilling::hole_order` (new module `drilling/order.rs`). The three arms of `generate` put the hole list in that order before the kernel reads it. The three kernels are not changed.
- The lathe's axial and cross holes refuse a pick. No XY order exists there.
- The picks ride the existing `EditOperationParams` and the existing `picks` field of #3339. No new command and no new file key.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/3328-drilling-hole-order.md`.

## Tests

Pins (all red before the fix, on unchanged `upstream/main` code at `ddee3aed6`):

- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::drill_cuts_the_picked_first_hole_and_last_hole` (golden `hole_order_drill.cl`)
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::bore_cuts_the_picked_first_hole_and_last_hole` (golden `hole_order_bore.cl`)
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::thread_cuts_the_picked_first_hole_and_last_hole_and_undo_restores_the_order` (golden `hole_order_thread.cl`; undo and redo of `EditOperationParams`)
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::a_pick_that_is_not_on_a_hole_is_refused_by_name` (the three kinds; the door and the generator; two picks on one hole)
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::a_pick_on_a_drill_with_cross_holes_is_refused_by_name`
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_hole_order_picks_and_undo_clears_them`
- `drilling_axial::a_start_or_exit_pick_on_the_axial_hole_refuses_by_name`
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::start_exit_rows::tests::the_hole_kinds_type_their_first_and_last_hole`
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `drilling::order::tests::*` (4 tests of the rule)

Red before the fix: the six `hole_order` pins failed. The order pins read `[20, 60, 100, 140]` (the list order). The other pins read `Drill: a start point is not taken - the planner chooses the entry and the exit of this kind until its slice of #1448 ships`.

title: DXF import: MPOLYGON and 3D surface records hidden in a non-drawing section are refused, not dropped
body:
## What changed

The DXF reader skips the sections that carry no geometry (CLASSES, ACDSDATA, THUMBNAILIMAGE) and refuses a file when a drawable record sits in one of them, so nothing is dropped silently. It knows a record is drawable from `ENTITY_KINDS` in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/entities.rs`. That list lacked `MPOLYGON` and the six SURFACE subtypes (`EXTRUDEDSURFACE`, `LOFTEDSURFACE`, `NURBSURFACE`, `PLANESURFACE`, `REVOLVEDSURFACE`, `SWEPTSURFACE`). They are on the list now (46 to 53 names).

`SUN` stays off the list on purpose. It is in the ENTITIES chapter of the DXF Reference, but AutoCAD writes it in OBJECTS (subclass `AcDbSun`, no `AcDbEntity`), and the OBJECTS reader refuses every kind on this list as "graphical entity in OBJECTS". Adding it would refuse real AutoCAD files with sun settings. A comment above the list says so.

## How tested

- New `dxf_classes_section::mpolygon_and_the_surface_kinds_in_a_section_without_geometry_are_refused`: each of the seven kinds in each of the three inert sections is a named refusal. It fails without the change.
- New `dxf_objects_section::a_sun_object_in_objects_stays_inert`: a SUN object in OBJECTS imports the same entities as the file without it.
- All DXF suites pass (`dxf`, `dxf_classes_section`, `dxf_objects_section`, `dxf_inert_sections`, `dxf_refusals`).
- `cargo xtask gate quick` on Windows: 1203 of 1206 steps pass, clippy clean. The three failures do not touch DXF and come from this checkout: `sinumerik_810m_post::air_cut_kit_posts_cleanly_and_matches_committed_kit` (the golden `.mpf` was checked out with CRLF line endings), `catalog_render::catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly` (`rough-finish`: "its file changed", the same line-ending cause) and `egui_app` (the test binary stops with an access violation, a GPU driver crash here).

## Not exercised

No real DXF file with MPOLYGON or a surface record in an inert section was opened; the tests use synthetic records.

Changelog: DXF import refuses a damaged file that hides an MPOLYGON or 3D surface record in a section without geometry, instead of dropping it silently.

body:

## Covered and remaining (#3662)

| #3662 item | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A tapered mill with a tip diameter or a ball tip | Covered on main by D1, PR #3929 (`tip_form`, `tip_diameter`, `.camtools` version 6) | `tool_library.rs::a_tip_form_round_trips_and_steps_the_version`; this PR adds the #3662 synthetic numbers: `converted_3662::the_3662_tapered_mills_round_trip_with_their_tips` |
| A drawn cutter outline in a `.camtools` definition | Covered on main by D3a, PR #3906 (`cutter`, version 5) | `tool_library.rs::a_drawn_cutter_round_trips_through_the_library_file` |
| A form mill with a drawn profile | Covered on main by D2, PR #3946 (`form_mill` with `form`) for outlines whose radius does not narrow upward | `tool_library.rs::a_form_mill_round_trips_with_its_outline` |
| The #3662 synthetic form mill (one V tooth on a necked shank) | Covered by this PR: it is a single-form thread mill with its drawn cutter | `converted_3662::the_3662_form_mill_rides_the_file_as_a_necked_single_form_thread_mill` |
| A single-form thread mill without a pitch range | This PR | see below |
| The dovetail neck check without a tolerance | This PR | see below |
| A general form mill whose outline narrows upward (an undercut form) | Remaining. `form_mill.rs` refuses it by name; the work stays with #896 | `form_mill.rs` module comment |
| Operations that cut with a flat-tip or ball-tip taper | Remaining, outside #3662 (which asks for the file only). The operation doors refuse such a tool by name (`taper::is_unread_tip`) | `taper.rs` module comment |

## What changed

- `camcraft_tools::thread_mill::read_unstated_range`: a single-form thread mill whose definition has no `pitch_min` key reads as a range of its one stated pitch (`pitch_min = pitch`). The thread operation then cuts that pitch and refuses every other pitch by name (the existing `resolve_pitch` door). This is the narrowest range. It never widens what an operation accepts.
- `ToolDto::pitch_min` is now `Option<f64>`. Only an absent key gets the one-pitch reading. A stated `pitch_min: 0` stays 0 and the sanity law refuses it by name, as before. So `edit_tool` cannot turn a stated 0 into another number. The writer is unchanged: it writes the key only when it is not 0.
- The shipped catalog reader (`catalog_asset.rs`) reads an absent key in the same way.
- `undercut.rs`: the dovetail neck check is `top < sr - NECK_MEETS`, with `NECK_MEETS = 1e-9` mm (float dust, the same slack as the lollipop check). The #3662 inch dovetail (0.24 in head, 0.0575 in high, 45 degrees, 1/8 in neck) puts its flank top one ulp under the neck in mm. It is now accepted. A neck 1e-6 mm or 0.002 mm wider is still refused.
- `camcraft-mcp` skill: the thread-mill row says what an absent `pitch_min` means.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3662-camtools-rest.md`.

## Version step

None. This build writes no new key and no new value: a single-form mill that it writes always states `pitch_min`. Thus each file that this build writes is read by older builds. An older build refuses only a file without the key (for example from a converter), by the tool's name, as it did before. No file that older builds read changes meaning, so the change is not breaking.

## Readings

- #3662 dovetail in mm: `0.24*25.4 = 6.095999999999999`, flank top `1.5874999999999995`, neck radius `1.5875`.
- #3662 form mill: diameter 8, flute length 1.6 (the tooth), pitch 1.6, form angle `2*atan(0.8/2) = 43.6` degrees, neck 2 mm radius from 1.6 to 9, shank 8 to 40. The thread operation refuses its 43.6 degree form by name.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft_tools::undercut::tests::a_neck_that_meets_the_flank_exactly_is_accepted`
- `camcraft_tools::thread_mill::tests::an_unstated_range_reads_as_the_one_stated_pitch`
- `camcraft_tools::catalog_asset::tests::a_catalog_single_form_thread_mill_without_a_range_cuts_its_one_pitch`
- `app tool_library::converted_3662::a_single_form_thread_mill_without_a_pitch_range_loads`
- `app tool_library::converted_3662::the_3662_form_mill_rides_the_file_as_a_necked_single_form_thread_mill`
- `app tool_library::converted_3662::the_3662_tapered_mills_round_trip_with_their_tips`

The new app tests are a module of the existing `tool_library` binary (`crates/app/tests/tool_library/converted_3662.rs`), as `tool_library_holders/used_by.rs` is. No new test binary.

## Not exercised

- No UI change. The tool editor still seeds a range when the kind is picked; it shows a no-range tool as finest = coarsest.
- No heavy step (P6, not P1).
- A thread toolpath with a one-pitch single-form mill is not generated here; the operation reads the same `resolve_pitch`, pinned in `thread_mill.rs`.

## Gate (Windows, winbuild)

Only the add of a tool took the catalog speed without a reading of the mounted machine. `apply_cutting_data` and the Feeds tab spindle row already say when the machine holds a speed. title: feat(geometry): import DXF splines and ellipses as tangent arcs
body:
## What changed

- **SPLINE and ELLIPSE import.** Before this change, a DXF drawing with one SPLINE or ELLIPSE stopped the whole import ("unsupported entity"). Now the DXF reader reads them (`crates/geometry/src/dxf/curves.rs`, `nurbs.rs`, `curve_fit.rs`, `biarc.rs`). It lays each curve as tangent-continuous circular arcs (biarcs) and lines. The output is ordinary `Line` and `Arc` primitives, so the chainer, the profile picks and the wire arc contour of #3937 read it with no change.
  - SPLINE: degree 1 to 11, knots, control points, weights (rational), fit-point count. Evaluation is de Boor in homogeneous coordinates.
  - ELLIPSE: centre, major axis, ratio, start and end parameter. A ratio of 1 gives an exact `Circle` or `Arc`.
  - A degree-1 spline gives its control polygon (split at each corner knot).
- **The tolerance and its side.** `CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM` = 0.001 mm, two-sided (Hausdorff). Each fitted piece is checked: each curve point is within 1 µm of the arcs, and each arc point is within 1 µm of the curve. Between the samples, a bound on the curve speed covers the curve side, and the unit speed of the arcs covers the arc side. Speed bound: the derivative control polygon (non-rational spline), `2p (wmax / wmin) D / span` (rational spline), the semi-major axis (ellipse). The output is on no fixed side of the curve. 1 µm is less than half of the wire cover law tolerance (2 µm). An arc with a radius above `CURVE_MAX_RADIUS_MM` (1000 mm) becomes a line, and the same check applies to it.
- **Units.** The bound is in millimetres. A drawing without `$INSUNITS` is read as inches (the largest unit the application lets a caller state), so the bound in drawing units is the tightest. `Document::curve_tolerance` keeps the used value. `SketchData::from_dxf` refuses (`SketchError::CurveTolerance`) when the applied unit makes the bound looser than 1 µm.
- **Refused by name, never clamped.** Degree, knot count, knot order, empty domain, knot multiplicity, weight count, zero / negative / non-finite weights, weight ratio over 1e6, control or fit points in two Z planes (an omitted Z is 0), an orphan or duplicate Z of a control or fit point, counts over the vertex limit (checked before the values are read), fit points without control points, ellipse ratio outside (0, 1], zero axis, zero sweep, parameter over 1e6, tilted axis or extrusion. A curve that needs more evaluations than the drawing budget (50 million) is refused before the work starts. A cusp that 40 halvings cannot fit is refused.
- **INSERT and POINT decision.** They do not stop the import now. Each is skipped and counted in `summary.skipped` (an INSERT with attributes takes its ATTRIB records up to SEQEND). Block expansion is not in this PR; it stays open on #1865. A selected-chain wire cut still refuses a drawing with a skipped INSERT or POINT by name, as for HATCH: the block geometry is not read, so its clearance from the wire cannot be checked.
- **Provenance cleanup (separate small item).** The provenance lines of `crates/post/src/agie/{mod,cutoff,group}.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`, `agie_setup/{cutoff,group,quality}.rs`, `agie_setup/inspection/piece.rs`, `docs/decisions/2966-agie-fine-quality.md`, and the licence section heading in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` and `site/static/icons/LICENSES.txt` no longer name the tool they came from. They say "our own implementation". The MIT licence text stays. The public sources that the lines also name stay.
- **Build fix carried.** `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs` on main does not compile (`WireContourOp` has no `start` field, #3952). This branch carries the same hunks as PR #3953 (by mkinney), so the suite builds. When #3953 merges first, the merge is clean.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/1865-dxf-spline-ellipse.md`.

## Readings

- Closed cubic SPLINE (fixture `crates/geometry/tests/dxf/spline.dxf`, about 80 mm long): 72 segments, measured Hausdorff 4.1e-4 mm against an independent Cox-de Boor evaluation (bound 1e-3 mm).
- The same spline as a wire die (hole at its centre, generic ISO wire post): 74 `G3` blocks, all laws clean (`verdict.findings` empty, slug captured).
- Unitless rational quarter circle of radius 10: at most 8 arcs, each point within 0.001 / 25.4 of the circle.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-geometry --test dxf`: `curves::closed_cubic_spline_reads_as_tangent_arcs_within_the_bound`, `curves::rational_quarter_circle_spline_becomes_arcs_on_its_circle`, `curves::degree_one_spline_is_its_control_polygon`, `curves::ellipses_read_as_tangent_arcs_and_a_round_one_stays_a_circle`, `curves::a_slender_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_at_its_tight_ends`, `curves::insert_and_point_are_skipped_and_the_rest_reads`.
- `camcraft-geometry --test dxf_refusals`: `curve_refusals::malformed_splines_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_refusals::malformed_ellipses_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_refusals::mutated_curve_records_never_panic` (300 fixed-seed mutations), `curve_refusals::curves_read_for_a_smaller_unit_than_the_applied_one_are_refused`, and the changed `dxf_unsupported_entities_are_refused_by_name` (INSERT now reads).
- `camcraft-app --test wire_dxf_selection`: `arcs::closed_spline_die_cuts_as_tangent_arcs_and_posts_its_golden` (new golden `wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc`), and `arcs::arcs_stay_refused_for_taper_and_a_hatch_still_blocks_the_cut` (now also an INSERT refusal).

## Goldens moved

None. One golden is new: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc`. The six goldens of #3937 and all other goldens are unchanged (the drawings without splines or ellipses read byte for byte as before).

## Not exercised

- No physical cut and no control run of a spline program.
- Sodick and G-EDM goldens for the spline (the arc blocks are the same code path as #3937).
- Splines with only fit points (refused), periodic splines whose control points do not wrap (they read as an open chain), and block expansion.
- Known output defect, filed as a follow-up: between two tangent arcs the wire arc path of #3937 adds a connector line of a few nanometres. On a biarc chain each joint is such a joint, so the program has a zero-length `G1` after each arc (72 in the new golden). The moves are safe, and the laws check them. The follow-up removes them.

## Review fixes (review of head `ed5d85de4`)

1. **Coordinate completeness (blocking).** Fixed by the reviewer in `62b3fdf17`. Each control point is X, Y and at most one Z. An omitted Z is 0. Orphan Z, duplicate Z and points in two Z planes are refused by name. Pinned by `curve_refusals::spline_control_points_use_a_per_point_z_default` and `curve_refusals::spline_control_points_refuse_orphan_and_duplicate_z`.
2. **Equal weights are found once (optional).** `Nurbs::new` sets `uniform` one time. `speed()` reads it and does not scan the weights for each span. 40,000 collinear control points (debug build): 13.8 s before, 0.5 s after. Pinned by `curve_bounds::a_long_non_rational_spline_reads_in_linear_time` (bound 5 s).
3. **Near-round ellipse (optional).** A ratio of exactly 1 is the exact circle, with no recorded tolerance. Below 1, the reader uses the circle only when `radius * (1 - ratio)` is within the tolerance in drawing units, and then records the tolerance. Otherwise it fits arcs. Pinned by `curve_bounds::a_near_round_ellipse_is_a_circle_only_within_the_tolerance` (both sides of the bound, and the review case at radius 1e10 mm).

Both `curve_bounds` tests failed on `62b3fdf17` and pass on `8973feb08`.

4. **Fit point elevation (same finding class as item 1).** Fixed in `1359ef98e`. The fit points (group codes 11/21/31) now follow the control point rule of `62b3fdf17`: each fit point is X, Y and at most one Z, and an omitted Z is 0. A Z before X and Y, a duplicate Z, a Y before X and an X with no Y are refused by name. All fit points and all control points must be in one Z plane, else the SPLINE is refused with "fit points are not in one Z plane". Before this fix, the reader ignored group codes 21 and 31, so a fit Z off the plane was not checked. Pinned by `curve_refusals::spline_fit_points_use_a_per_point_z_default` (a fit-only spline with one explicit Z of 1 and one omitted Z, in both orders; all omitted reads at 0; all equal explicit reads at 2; a mixed fit Z and a fit plane that differs from the control plane are refused) and `curve_refusals::spline_fit_points_refuse_orphan_and_duplicate_z`. Both tests failed on `8973feb08` and pass on `1359ef98e`.

## Gate

On head `1359ef98e` (the fit point fix):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1206 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 30.3 min. The plan holds every app suite (the `example_catalog*` suites included), `wire_dxf_selection`, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, the ui suites and the clippy step.
- Strict clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Light lane: `cargo xtask gate light --only "motion light" --only "app light"`: 5 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- The branch merges cleanly with `origin/main` (`97a676e5c`), so no merge commit was necessary.

On head `8973feb08` the same three commands were green (quick: 1206 steps, 0 failed, wall 30.2 min).

Heavy: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches 106 steps (geometry is shared). This issue is `P4`, not `P1`, so no heavy step runs ("Heavy lanes at review").

## Review fix

- SPLINE import checks each control point when the next point starts or the record ends. An omitted Z is zero for that point. The reader rejects an orphan or duplicate Z and rejects points in different Z planes.
- `spline_control_points_use_a_per_point_z_default` covers a missing Z in both orders. It also covers zero and equal explicit elevations. `spline_control_points_refuse_orphan_and_duplicate_z` covers orphan, out-of-order and duplicate Z fields.
- Pin proof. Both tests failed on `ed5d85de4` with the new tests and the old parser. Both passed with the fix. `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test dxf --test dxf_refusals` passed all 44 tests.

### Gates on `62b3fdf174b4c02278ce03fa1c2e5d4ee33c7e25`

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran 1,206 steps. 1,203 passed, 3 failed, and 0 stalled. The red steps were `ui suites: lib`, `ui suites: egui_app`, and `ui suites: shell`. They match the missing graphics adapter failures from the prior review.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` ran 106 steps. 105 passed, 1 failed, and 0 stalled. The red step was `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`. The test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` read counts of 4,688 moves, 4,660 planar moves, and 1,980 fitted arcs. Its pin expects 3,158, 3,130, and 1,141. The same release test failed with the same counts and diagnostic when run with the original parser from `ed5d85de4`.
- Both gate commands started against upstream main `d94b9816d`. Upstream advanced during the runs. The merge base with the fix stayed at `98caf2dfd`, so the selected diff stayed the same.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. The quick gate also passed its batch Clippy step.
- The debug example catalog passed 41 tests. The heavy catalog passed its other 4 tests. The adaptive and edge-work catalog suites also passed. The conformance (7), solid-law (7), wire DXF (7), and wire decimal (2) suites passed.

### Goldens moved in this fix

None. The catalog and golden suites passed. The spline die golden already in the PR passed its byte comparison.

No physical cut was run. The fix changes the DXF reader and tests, so there are no UI screenshots.

Effort: high (the issue is labelled `effort:max`; this PR is its SPLINE and ELLIPSE part).

title: fix(wire): Wire Contour takes an exit pick
body:
## What changed

Wire Contour takes an exit pick (`picks.exit`), beside its threading point (`picks.start`).

- `PickCapability::Threading` takes a start and an exit. `list_operation_types` and the `edit_operation` schema say so.
- An open run: the cut ends at the end of the run nearest the exit pick. The wire rides the same line on the same side. The walk turns round when the pick names the first end.
- A closed profile: the cut is the automatic cut, all the way round from the threading point. The wire then rides its own kerf on, in the same direction, to the point of the path nearest the pick. It leaves by a straight lead-out to the pick. It does not return to the threading point.
- The exit is a new module, `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/exit.rs`. It runs the existing generator first, then reads the exit. A cut without an exit pick does not enter the module.

Refused by name, never moved:

- An exit pick the same distance from the two ends of an open run.
- An exit pick on the wire path, nearer the profile than the kerf offset, or on the product side (outside a die, inside a punch).
- An exit pick with tabs, skims, a taper, a no-core burnout or a 4-axis cut. The command door refuses the pair, and generation refuses it again.
- An exit pick on a selected DXF chain that is cut on its own arcs.

## Cause

`PickCapability::Threading::takes` accepted the start role only. The command door refused each exit pick on a Wire Contour: "Wire Contour: a exit point is not taken - this kind takes a start point only". The wire generators had no input for an exit.

PR #3871 already moved `WireContourOp.start` into `picks` and reads the old `start` key. This PR adds the parts that the sweep comment on the issue lists as open.

## Where the issue is silent (smallest change chosen)

The decision file `docs/decisions/3332-wire-exit-pick.md` has the reasons.

- Closed profile: the wire rides on in the lap's own direction, as the 2D Contour ring does. It does not take the shorter way.
- Tabs: the issue says "before the tab or the cut-off". This PR refuses an exit pick with tabs by name. Each stretch between tabs and the tab cut-off start from the threading point with the wire threaded. An exit before the cut-off needs a second threading, and the post has no word for it.
- 4-axis: the pair is refused by name, so the sync pair rule holds without a change.
- A start pick on an open run is ignored, as before this PR. This PR does not change it.
- The Wire Contour Geometry tab shows the exit coordinates. The user can set, edit, and clear the draft exit. Apply commits through the command history.

## Tests

Pins (all red before the fix, except the load test):

- `crates/app/tests/wire_post/exit_pick.rs` (in the existing `wire_post` binary):
  - `an_exit_pick_on_an_open_run_ends_the_cut_at_the_end_nearest_the_pick`
  - `an_exit_pick_between_the_ends_of_an_open_run_is_refused_by_name`
  - `an_exit_pick_on_a_closed_profile_leaves_the_cut_at_the_pick`
  - `each_exit_pick_the_wire_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`
  - `undo_and_redo_restore_the_path_of_an_exit_pick`
  - `a_file_with_the_old_start_key_opens_to_the_same_path`
- `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/exit_pick.rs`: `a_polygon_chain_is_left_at_the_exit_pick_and_passes_the_wire_laws`, `a_chain_cut_on_its_arcs_refuses_the_exit_pick_by_name`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_wire_contour.rs`: `edit_operation_sets_the_wire_exit_pick_and_refuses_one_it_cannot_hold`.
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/exit_tests.rs`: 5 unit tests of the module.
- Changed on purpose: `start_exit_shared::every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` asserted that the wire refuses an exit. It now asserts that the wire takes it.

Red before the fix. On unchanged `upstream/main` (`98caf2dfd`), 5 of the 6 `wire_post::exit_pick` tests failed with:

```
invalid parameters: Wire Contour: a exit point is not taken - this kind takes a start point only; clear it on this operation
```

`a_file_with_the_old_start_key_opens_to_the_same_path` passed before the fix. PR #3871 already reads the old key. The test is the load test that the issue asks for, not a red pin.

Mutation results (one guard removed, pins run, guard restored, pins green again):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `Threading` takes a start only (the old capability) | red: 5 `wire_post::exit_pick`, 2 `wire_dxf_selection::exit_pick`, the MCP pin, `start_exit_shared` |
| Door refusal of the pairs off | red: `each_exit_pick_the_wire_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`, the MCP pin |
| `generate_wire` ignores the exit pick (the old dispatch) | red: 5 `wire_post::exit_pick`, the polygon DXF pin, the MCP pin |
| Arcs refusal off | red: `a_chain_cut_on_its_arcs_refuses_the_exit_pick_by_name` |
| Tie guard off (motion) | red: `an_exit_pick_that_names_no_end_of_an_open_run_is_refused` |
| Exit side law off (motion) | red: `each_exit_pick_a_closed_profile_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name` |
| Tabs guard off (motion) | red: the same test |
| On-path guard off (motion) | red: the same test |
| Open run never turned (motion) | red: `an_open_run_ends_at_the_end_nearest_the_exit_pick` |
| Closed ride skipped (motion) | red: `a_closed_profile_is_cut_all_the_way_round_and_left_at_the_exit_pick`, `the_ride_to_the_exit_follows_the_lap` |
| Generation guard of the pairs off (door still on) | **green: no pin** |

title: fix(xtask): warn when the gate base branch is behind its remote
body:
## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate quick` and `cargo xtask gate heavy` now check the base branch.
- The check compares the local `<base>` with `upstream/<base>` and `origin/<base>`.
- For each remote copy that has commits the local branch lacks, the gate prints one warning line.
- The line gives the count of commits and the `--base` value to use.
- The gate plan does not change. The check only warns.
- The check uses the refs of the last `git fetch`. It does not fetch.
- New module `xtask/src/stale_base.rs`. One call in `changed_since` in `xtask/src/main.rs`. Quick and heavy share that function.

Example from this worktree, with the default base `main`:

```
warning: the local 'main' is 2230 commits behind 'upstream/main' (as of the last fetch): the diff can hold files that this branch did not change. Use --base upstream/main after git fetch.
warning: the local 'main' is 1002 commits behind 'origin/main' (as of the last fetch): the diff can hold files that this branch did not change. Use --base origin/main after git fetch.
changed since main (f2d78f3): 3265 file(s)
```

## Cause

Worktree agents do not pull in the main checkout (#1201). Thus the local `main` can be far behind. The gate diffed against it with no message. The diff held many files that the branch did not change, and quick fell back to batch.

## Tests

- Pins (in `xtask/src/stale_base_tests.rs`, a throw-away repository with fake remote refs):
  - `stale_base_tests::gate_warns_when_local_main_is_behind_origin`
  - `stale_base_tests::stale_base_warning_text_counts_commits`
- Red before the fix: yes. With the old behaviour (no warning), the main pin fails: `assertion left == right failed: only origin/main is ahead: []`.
- Mutations, each run against the pins, then restored:
  - No warning (the old behaviour): red.
  - Reversed range (`theirs..local`): red.
  - Warn at zero (`behind >= 0`): red (both pins).
  - Restored code: green.
- Quick gate on the final head: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` gives 1 step, `xtask unit tests`, ok in 154 s, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `watchdog_tests::a_silent_step_is_killed_as_a_tree_and_named`, which passes outside the sandbox.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: one error, in `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` (`clippy::needless_bool`). This PR does not touch that file. The error is on upstream/main on macOS, where the `#[cfg(windows)]` block is compiled out. No clippy finding is in the files of this PR.

## Goldens moved

None. The change is in `xtask/` only. No post, toolpath or catalog code changed, so the catalog suites and the heavy lanes do not apply.

## Not exercised

- A real `git fetch`. The test sets the remote refs with `git update-ref`.
- Windows and Linux. The check uses only `git rev-list --count`, so it has no platform code.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `xtask/src/`.

Process change: yes

title: fix(3d): rapid to the plunge height before a pocket restart, merge sub-resolution feeds
body:
Stacked on #3880 (merge #3880 first).

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs`: a pass that restarts after a hop with a straight plunge now calls `descent::feed_down`. The tool goes down by a rapid to the plunge height over the material. Then it feeds the rest. Before, it fed the whole way from the hop plane.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs`: `feed_down` is now `pub(super)`. The code does not change.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/short_moves.rs` (new): `merge_short_feeds` merges each straight feed that moves less than 0.001 mm on every axis into its straight neighbour. A short move with no straight feed beside it stays. The chain of moves stays unbroken. `ladder` calls it on the finished path when the path has no compensation spans.
- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish`: made again with `cargo xtask catalog --case 3d/rough-finish`.
- `docs/decisions/3852-pocket-restart-rapid.md`: the choices and what was dropped.

## Cause

1. The restart branch in `ladder` pushed a rapid to the hop plane and then one plunge to the level. It did not use the plunge-height rapid that the level entry uses.
2. Offset-ring vertices that are almost the same point gave feed moves shorter than 0.001 mm. The post wrote them as `G01` blocks with the same X, Y and Z as the block before them.

Note: after #3857 (ea39d4180), the catalog case posts no restart plunge. Its restarts take the ramp. The straight-plunge branch is still reached when the entry is Plunge, or when no entry fits. The motion pin uses that path.

## Tests

Pins:

Mutations:

- Put back the old straight plunge in `ladder`: the motion pin is red (the same 13.5 mm message). Restored: green.
- Turn off the `merge_short_feeds` call: `catalog_3d_rough_finish::regenerates` is red. After `cargo xtask catalog --case 3d/rough-finish`, the catalog pin is red (18 zero-length moves). Restored: all 6 `catalog_3d_rough_finish` tests are green.

title: fix(tools): a short-flute meridian steps out to the full radius
body:
## What changed

- `Tool::meridian()` adds the radial shoulder `(flute_len, diameter / 2)` when a flute ends before the tip reaches the full radius.
- The cone arm (sharp taper, drill) gets the shoulder. This is the case that the issue names.
- The short-flute branch of `tip_arc` (ball nose, bull nose) gets the same shoulder. The issue's "Done means" asks for every tool kind, and this branch has the same gap.
- The meridian now ends where `Tool::profile` ends. This is the rule that #3929 gave the flat and ball taper tips.
- The shoulder is added only when it is at least `MIN_LEN` (1e-6 mm). A tool whose flute reaches the full radius keeps the same meridian points, bit for bit.
- `a_sharp_taper_keeps_its_profile_and_digest` pinned the old short-flute meridian (`Taper 10 mm, 30 deg, flute 5`). Its expected points now include the shoulder. The profile and the `same_shape` checks in that test do not change.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3938-cone-shoulder.md`.

## Cause

The cone arm pushed `(fl, r)` only when `fl > top`. A short flute has `fl == top`, so the meridian ended at `(fl, fl * tan)`. `Tool::profile` always adds `(zc, r)` at the flute top. `tip_arc` ended a short ball or bull flute on the arc in the same way.

## Who reads the meridian

- No production code calls `Tool::meridian()` today. Only tests in `camcraft-tools` and `camcraft-sim` read it.
- So no toolpath, posted program or collision verdict changes now. The fix stops a later reader (the sub-issues of #3351) from seeing a smaller tool than the profile.
- The shoulder is a flat segment. `Meridian::atoms` makes no atom from a flat segment. The solid law pairing `meridian_atoms_match_cutter_atoms_for_each_mill_kind` (sim) stays green with no change.

## Tests (final head 55fda4df5)

- Pin: `meridian::tests::a_short_flute_meridian_has_the_profile_shoulder` (camcraft-tools lib). It covers a sharp taper, a drill, a ball nose, a bull nose, an end mill and a T-slot. It checks that the meridian ends at the profile's flute top, that the cone still ends at the flute top, and that no atom has zero height.
- Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged source: `left: Some((5.0, 1.3397459621556136)) right: Some((5.0, 5.0))`.
- Mutation 1: revert the cone guard to `if fl > top`. The pin is red (with `a_sharp_taper_keeps_its_profile_and_digest`). Restore: green.
- Mutation 2: disable the `tip_arc` shoulder. The pin is red. Restore: green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1 step (`tools suites: lib`), ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --tests`: all suites ok.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib`: 249 passed.
- Heavy (P1, safety floor, one targeted step): `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --only "app heavy: tool_body" --only "app heavy: verify"`: 2 steps, ok (387 s, 3 s). No heavy test reads `Tool::meridian()`. The reach (105 steps) comes only from the crate dependency, so the whole lane was not run (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").
- Example catalog: `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: 3 steps, ok.

## Goldens moved

None. The three example catalog suites ran on the final head and passed. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Not exercised

- The bull-nose profile clamps the corner radius to a short flute, so it draws a different arc under the flute top than the meridian. The two agree at the flute top after this fix. The arc below is out of scope.
- The solid law (`Cutter::atoms`) has no disc at the flute top. A zero-height shoulder has no volume, so it was not changed.
- The full heavy lanes were not run (see above).

## Overlaps

- #3946 touches `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs` and `meridian_tests.rs`. It changes other lines of `Tool::meridian()` (a form-mill branch and the input check), not the cone arm or `tip_arc`. Whichever PR merges second refreshes.

`crates/tools/src/meridian_tests.rs` is 403 lines (371 before).

Changelog: The tool meridian of a sharp taper, a drill, a ball nose or a bull nose with a short flute now steps out to the full radius at the flute top, as the tool profile does.

title: feat(tools): a form mill kind with roundover, cove, ogee, V-groove and bead presets
body:
Stacked on #3929 (D1, taper tip form). The D2 commits only: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/compare/f2fff2b3f1ef4586f09d0e8db96d1c6760ebc62c...qsmits:Camcraft:issue/3369-form-mill-presets

Plan step D2 of the tool library redesign (#3663).

## What changed

- **New kind `ToolKind::FormMill`** (file word `form_mill`). Its cutting edge is the outline in the new field `Tool::form` (`FormSpec`: points `[z, r, arc]` from the tip up, `pilot_len`, and the preset that wrote the points). New module `crates/tools/src/form_mill.rs` with `form_mill_presets.rs`.
- **Presets** write the outline from router bit catalogue numbers:
  - roundover: radius, pilot radius, cutting height;
  - cove: radius, pilot radius, cutting height;
  - ogee: two radii, the step, pilot radius, cutting height;
  - V-groove: included angle, tip radius, cutting diameter, cutting height (no pilot);
  - bead: radius, step (the quirk), pilot radius, cutting height.
- **Pilot band**: the segments up to `pilot_len` (the tip face and the bearing side) are non-cutting in the meridian. The bearing has its own radius.
- **The outline sets the diameter and the flute length.** `is_sane` refuses a disagreement by name and states the correct numbers. The editor and MCP call `Tool::settle_form`. A file load does not repair a disagreement: it refuses it.
- **Undercut refused by name**: an outline whose radius narrows upward is refused with a reference to #896.
- `Tool::meridian` and `Tool::profile` read the outline. `profile` flattens the arcs on the outside of the cutter (the spun-profile law), so the collision band stack is never smaller than the form. `cutter_fit::same_shape` compares the form, and the operation stamp hashes the whole outline and the pilot.
- **Operation doors**: the form mill is in the `CONE` family, so `no_orphan_tool_kinds` stays green. `tool_gate` refuses it by name for each operation (creation, edit, re-tool, generation and post). The 2D Chamfer refusal names the edge form work (#896). No refusal suggests a form mill, and no operation offers one.
- **Catalog**: `FM-RO-R6`, `FM-RO-R0250IN`, `FM-CV-R6`, `FM-CV-R0250IN`, `FM-VG-90-12`, `FM-VG-90-0500IN` (roundover, cove and 90-degree V-groove, in mm and inch). The catalog states the preset; the reader writes the points. The inch roundover and cove state their true inch numbers: a 3/16 in pilot, `0.1875 * 25.4` = 4.7625 mm, and a 11/16 in flute length, 17.4625 mm (not rounded values). The sanity law compares the outline with the diameter and flute length with a slack of `AGREE` = 1e-6 mm (1 nm); the holder stack test compares the spun stack with the cylinder with a slack of 1e-9 mm, not exact float equality (a 17.4625 mm flute under a 32 mm shank gives a 25.000000000000007 mm holder band).
- **Editor**: "Form mill" in the type list; a "Form preset" list (a drawn outline or one of the five presets), the preset number rows and the pilot length (`tool_form_mill_row.rs`, called from `kind_rows()`); diameter and flute length are shown, not typed. The shape window's Draw cutter view names the form in place of a tip number. New original icon `tool-form-mill` (SVG master and PNG).
- **MCP**: `add_tool` and `edit_tool` take `form` (preset or drawn points, and `pilot_len`); descriptions, `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the `camcraft-mcp` skill row updated. The cutter tools read the form through `Tool::profile`; a diameter edit that leaves the outline is refused by name.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3369-form-mill-presets.md`. The main decision: the outline lives on `Tool`, not only in `ToolCutter`, because the catalog, the meridian, `Tool::profile` and the sanity law see only `Tool`.

## Version steps

None. Only the `form_mill` kind states a `form`, and each older build (D1 included) refuses the unknown kind word by name, so it cannot read a form mill as another tool. A project or library without a form mill is unchanged. The library test pins that a form mill library stays under `TIP_FORM_VERSION`. Not marked breaking: this follows the additive kind words of #1444 (T-slot, keyseat, dovetail, lollipop).

## Readings

- Catalogue diameters from the meridian: FM-RO-R6 25.0 mm, FM-RO-R0250IN 25.4 mm, FM-CV-R6 25.0 mm, FM-CV-R0250IN 25.4 mm, FM-VG-90-12 12.0 mm, FM-VG-90-0500IN 12.7 mm.
- Ogee R4 / R3, step 1.5, pilot radius 6.35: cuts at radius 14.85 mm. Bead R6.35, step 1.6, pilot radius 6.35: 14.3 mm.
- Dialog: a roundover radius edit from 6 to 8 mm gives diameter 29.0 mm after Apply (one undo step).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-tools` lib: `form_mill::tests::{each_preset_meets_its_catalogue_radius, the_pilot_band_does_not_cut, bad_preset_numbers_are_refused_by_name, an_undercut_outline_is_refused_by_name, the_outline_owns_the_diameter_and_the_kind_owns_the_form, the_side_view_never_falls_inside_the_form, a_number_edit_keeps_the_drawn_form, the_wire_form_round_trips}`, `catalog_asset_tests::the_catalog_form_mills_cut_at_their_catalogue_diameter` (pins the true inch pilot and flute length and the point count of each preset: a sharp V-groove has two points, the tip on the axis and the top of the cone), `spun::tests::a_parametric_holder_stacks_as_the_cylinder` (renamed from `..._bit_identically_...`; slack 1e-9 mm). The `#[test]` count does not change.
- `camcraft-app` `tool_law`: `no_orphan_tool_kinds` (green with the new kind), `form_mill_is_refused_by_every_door`.
- `camcraft-app` `tool_library`: `a_form_mill_round_trips_with_its_outline` (library file, project file byte for byte, `ChangeTool` keeps the outline, refused diameter, preset without points).
- `camcraft-app` `mcp_edit_tool`: `add_and_edit_tool_take_a_form_mill_preset`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `tool_library_editor::{the_form_mill_presets_show, a_form_mill_profile_tab_names_its_form}`, `tool_form_mill_row::tests::{each_preset_seeds_a_sane_tool, another_kind_clears_the_form}`.
