U6 of the tool library redesign (#3663). The tool library window gets a Holders page: the built-in holders by spindle taper and a read-only holder view. This PR also closes the five gaps between U1 to U5 and the mock-up of #3663 (the scope comments on #3897).

Stacked on #3935 (U5). The commits of this PR only: https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/b82b017bb...issue/3897-tool-holders-list

Update: #3931 and #3935 merged into `main` (#3935 at its head `b82b017bb`, the base of this branch). The PR diff against `main` now shows the U6 commits only. The gate below merged origin/main `b13ebd440`, before those merges. GitHub reports the PR as mergeable with the current `main` (`02d05bc1c`).

## Two commits, two subjects
The UI refit rule asks for one page or component in each PR. The user decided to fold the mock-up gaps into U6, because each PR is costly on this project. So the PR keeps the rule by commit:
1. `dd129ab43` `feat(ui): close the tool library window's gaps to the mock-up`: the five layout items, their tests and the updated `layout_window_tool_*` tests. It does not build alone, by a split error (see the gate).
2. `3c622f8e5` `feat(ui): browse the holder library in the tool library window`: the Holders page, the used-by query in app, their tests and `layout_window_holders`.

The two belong together because they change the same window: the page switch heads the window, and the wider window and the two-column editor are the frame that the Holders page and the holder view use.

## What changed
Mock-up gaps (commit 1), all display only, no command:
1. **Editor layout.** The tabs and their rows stand on the left, the preview on the right (mock-up picture 2). U3 put the preview above the tabs.
2. **Preview toggles.** "Dimensions" and "Holder" check boxes beside the 3D / Side toggle (view state in `EditorFace`, both on). Holder off: the 3D view shows the model without the holder (`ToolModel::bare`, built with the model), and the side view shows no holder bands and no holder dimension. Dimensions off: the side view draws no dimension line. The flutes toggle comes with #3908.
3. **List rows.** Each Document row starts with a small drawing of the tool (`tool_library_dialog/thumbs.rs`: cached by the tool name and keyed on the tool value; a still frame only moves the kept shapes). A new "Gauge length" column shows the holder's gauge length plus the stick-out for a tool in a library holder. A tool with a drawn body, a mesh body or the stand-in cylinder shows "-", because its gauge line is not stated.
4. **Categories.** U2 did not add them. A column on the left of the list (`categories.rs`) groups the tools by kind under Milling, Hole making, Turning and Other, each category with its count (mock-up picture 1). A category with no tool in the shown source is not listed. A pick filters the rows, as the Tool type choice does (which stays).
5. **Window width.** The window opens `WIDE_W` wide (rail 170 + rows 780 + preview 320 + margins = 1330 px), so the Recipes table and the preview show side by side without a horizontal scroll bar. The window stands left of the Properties pane. On a narrower screen it takes the room left of Properties (it then covers the browser), and the Recipes table scrolls across as before. The minimum width is the same width.

Review fix (commit 3, `29af2e3e1`, the review of `3c622f8e5`):
- On a narrow window the rail folds from 170 px to 120 px (`rail_w`). The preview keeps 250 px while the rows keep 280 px (`columns`).
- The side view's dimension room gives way before the drawing (`side_view::margins`). With Dimensions off, the room is a thin 8 px border. With Dimensions on, the room shrinks in proportion, so the drawing keeps 96 px (`MIN_DRAW`). The painter clips a dimension value at the edge of the area.
- On a 960 px screen the drawing now paints. Before the fix, the side view took its early return and drew nothing.

Holders page (commit 2):
- A "Cutting tools | Holders" switch heads the window. The mock-up says "Tools". "Tools" is already the ribbon cell that opens the window (two buttons of one name break each test and MCP flow that clicks it), and "Tool list" is a browser row. See the decision file.

Columns: Name, Taper, Clamp, Clamps Ø, Gauge length, Largest Ø, Used by. A taper column on the left ("All holders" and each taper with its count), a name filter, and a note on the mounted machine's taper.
- `tool_library_dialog/holder_view.rs`: the read-only holder view (mock-up picture 5). Machine side (spindle taper, marked when it is the machine's), tool side (clamp and clamping range), shape (gauge length, largest diameter, nose diameter), "Used by N tools" with each tool's stick-out and gauge length (a click opens the tool in the editor), and the outline to scale with its dimension lines and a Dimensions toggle. The outline's shapes and labels are cached on the holder, the rect, the unit and the toggle.
- The view says: "Built-in holders are read-only. User holders and holder edits come with the user library (#3645)." "New holder", Import, Export, edit boxes, Duplicate and Apply on a holder are U7 (#3898).
- App: `tool_body::holder_users(world)` and `tool_body::tools_using_holder(world, entry)`, keyed on `HolderRef::entry` (case and spacing ignored, as `holder_library::find`). A read of the world, so it is in app.

Commands: none. Browsing, the toggles and the picks are view state. No MCP tool is owed: `get_job` already shows each tool's `holder.library`.

Seeded document, the end mill `EM-0600-4FL` put in `BT40 ER32` with the defaults: the list shows "1 tool" on the BT40 ER32 row, and the holder view lists the tool with its stick-out and gauge length. title: fix(wire): cut DXF arcs and circles as true arcs
body:
## What changed

A Wire Contour on a selected DXF chain with an arc or a circle now cuts. The wire path holds true arcs. The generic ISO, Sodick and G-EDM wire posts write them as G2 / G3 with incremental I J. An exact straight polygon keeps the polygon path of #3180, byte for byte.

### Motion (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/`)

- New `arc_span.rs`, `arc_chain.rs`: the closed line / arc / circle chain in world XY, walked counter-clockwise. The joint gap tolerance is `JOINT_TOL` = 0.25 µm. A wider gap is refused by name.
- New `arc_offset.rs`: the analytic offset. Each line moves along its normal. Each arc becomes a concentric arc. A pivot arc of the kerf radius about the drawing corner closes each outside corner. A trim at the meet of the two parallels closes each inside corner.
- Refusals by name, never a clamp:
- New `arc_cut.rs` (`wire_contour_arcs`): a straight lead to the nearest path point. On a circle the lead is radial. A full circle (or an arc of more than half a turn) is cut as two halves. Each arc goes onto its CL lattice centre (1e-6 mm) with its radius kept. If the centre move, the joint gap and the near-tangent miss together pass 1 nm, the path moves that far to the waste side, and a path note says so.
- New `arc_laws.rs`: the kerf law and the cover law read the drawing itself. The kerf law uses the exact least distance from each recorded move (line, or arc about its lattice centre) to each line and arc of the chain. `laws.rs` only moves the cover refusal text into `uncovered()` (no behaviour change).

### Sim verifier (`crates/sim/src/verify/wire/`)

- New `arcs.rs`: an XY arc move of a vertical cut is read as chords of at most 25 nm sagitta (`ARC_SAG`). Each chord reading is reduced by the chord's sagitta, so an arc whose kerf enters the product never passes.
- An arc on a leaning wire (taper) stays unreadable by name. A tabbed cut with arcs is unreadable by name.

### App (`crates/app/src/operation/`)

- `wire_sketch.rs`: the arc refusal and the exact-gap refusal are removed. `check_path` accepts XY arcs and bounds them by their axis extremes.
- New `wire_sketch_arcs.rs`: routes each chain that is not an exact polygon to `wire_contour_arcs`. The verifier gets the product as a waste-side ring of the chain within 25 nm. `single_pass` still refuses taper, tabs, skims, burnout and 4-axis on a selected chain.
- `generate.rs`, `wire_verify.rs`: the calls to the new routes.

### Post

- No post script changed. `crates/post/src/agie_setup/inspection.rs:1`: the provenance line now says "our own implementation".

## The user's decisions (24 Nov 2026)

1. True arcs, no chord-only step.
2. A start hole exactly at the centre of a die circle: the lead enters towards +X. Rule: of equally near path points, the point at the least counter-clockwise angle from +X wins. A path note says so.
3. **Behaviour change for the maintainer:** TEXT, MTEXT and DIMENSION entities no longer block a selected-chain wire cut. They are not cut, and the wire is not checked against them. A path note gives the count. A HATCH (or any other skipped entity) still refuses, now by its name and count. The native Agie selected-chain door shares this check, so it also accepts a drawing with annotation.
4. Tapered (conical) arcs stay refused. Follow-up: #3941.

A punch on a circle, a racetrack or a tangent loop also takes the arc path now for the generic posts (before: a chord preview). The native Agie job (#2978, #2993) still reads its own `WireProfile`, and its goldens do not change.

**Refusal order for a selected Agie chain (review fix).** The arc door now runs before the native door for each selected chain that is not an exact polygon, also on the Agie machine. Thus the arc door's start-hole and kerf laws can refuse before the native "convex loop" refusal. Example: a lower half circle that encloses the start hole now gives "lies inside the profile". Each refusal is correct, and nothing is published. The decision file records this order.

## Readings

I read the ISO golden `wire_dxf_die_circle.nc` against the drawing (radius 5 circle, wire 0.25, gap 0.04, k = 0.165; drawing centre posts at X6 Y5):

- the lead goes from X6 Y5 to X10.835 Y5: +X, length 4.835 = 5 - 0.165;
- `G3 X1.165 Y5. I-4.835 J0.`: centre X6 Y5, end at the antipode, counter-clockwise half turn;
- `G3 X10.835 Y5. I4.835 J0.`: centre X6 Y5, back to the seam;
- `G1 X6. Y5.`: the lead-out.

I read `wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc` (the L punch, drawing turned 90 degrees): the fillet posts as `G3 X13. Y15.165 I-3.165 J0.`, centre X13 Y12 (the drawn centre), radius 3 + 0.165. Each of the four sharp outside corners has a G3 pivot of radius 0.165 about the corner. The inside corner is trimmed to X5.835 Y5.165 (k, k from the corner). The walk is counter-clockwise. The Sodick program starts the cut with a `G01` lead before its first `G03`.

## Pinning tests

title: feat(tools)!: a tapered mill has a tip form (sharp, flat, ball)
body:
Plan step D1 of the tool library redesign (#3663). A tapered mill (`ToolKind::Taper`) states its tip form: sharp, flat or ball. The tip math is the research of #895.

## What changed

- **Tool fields.** `Tool` gets `tip_form` (`TaperTip`: `Sharp`, `Flat`, `Ball`; default `Sharp`) and `tip_diameter` (default 0). `corner_r` is the corner radius of a flat tip and the ball radius of a ball tip.
- **Tip math in a new module, `crates/tools/src/taper.rs`.** It holds the tip geometry (`r_flat`, `r_t`, `z_t`, `r0` of #895), the sanity rules by name, the drawn profile and the meridian. `Tool::profile`, `Tool::meridian` and `Tool::why_not_sane` call it. `tools.rs` grows by the field lines and one call. `Tool::geom` does not change: its numbers do not depend on the tip.
- **A sharp taper does not change.** Its profile, meridian and stamp stay bit for bit. Its corner radius stays inert, so an older project with such a tool still opens.
- **Only a chamfer mill states a tip.** Another kind with a non-sharp form or a tip diameter is refused by name. The editor clears the tip fields when the kind changes.
- **Every operation refuses a flat or ball tip by name**, until a generator reads it:
  - at creation, edit and re-tool (`tool_gate::tool_refusal`);
  - at generation and at the post (`tool_gate::tool_problem`). This second door catches a `ChangeTool` that gives the tool of an existing operation a flat tip.
  - The fitting-tool list and the catalog hint do not offer a flat or ball tip. The tool stamp digests the tip form and the tip diameter only for a non-sharp tip.
  - The text: `'CM-0600-90' has a flat tip: the tip form is not read by a Deburr operation yet - use a chamfer mill with a sharp tip`.
- **Files and MCP.** `ToolDto` and the catalog `Def` carry the two fields with `serde(default, skip_serializing_if)`. `add_tool` and `edit_tool` take them through `ToolDto`. `set_tool_cutter_params` takes `tip_form` and `tip_diameter`. `edit_tool` does not call `"tip_form": "sharp"` a lost key. The MCP reference (`docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`) has the new description.
- **Catalog.** Three new tools, common sizes from the public tapered end mill tables: `CM-0600-90-F10` (a flat-tip chamfer mill), `TE-0250-03-F10` (a tapered flat end mill) and `TB-0160-01-R05` (a tapered ball nose).
- **UI.** The Tool tab and Properties show a "Tip form" row for a chamfer mill, and a "Tip diameter" row for a flat tip (new `tool_taper_tip_row.rs`). The edit lands through `ChangeTool` / `AddTool`: one undo step.

## The two version steps (isolated, can be removed)

The user decided on 24 Nov 2026 to step the project-file version too. An older CamCraft reads a flat or ball tip as sharp. A sharp tip is a smaller tool than the real tool, and a toolpath planned for it can gouge. The issue text says "no version step", and the maintainer has not answered the comment on #3368 yet. The user said: "Just start, we can refactor that version step in or out later."

- **`.camproj`**: only a file with a flat or ball tip says `TIP_FORM_PROJECT_VERSION` (79). A file without one still says `PROJECT_VERSION` (78), so an older build opens it as before. This build reads 79 as 78 plus the tip keys.
  - The step is isolated in `crates/app/src/project/file.rs`: `TIP_FORM_PROJECT_VERSION`, `NEWEST_PROJECT_VERSION`, `written_project_version` and `tip_form_read_version`. There is one call in `wire.rs` (save) and one call in `apply.rs` (load).
  - A const assertion stops a later unconditional step from taking 79 by accident.
  - The nine tests that ask for a refused future version now use `NEWEST_PROJECT_VERSION + 1`.
  - To remove the step: delete the four items, write `PROJECT_VERSION` in `wire.rs`, remove the `apply.rs` line, and set the future-version tests back to `PROJECT_VERSION + 1`.
- **`.camtools`**: a library with a flat or ball tip says `TIP_FORM_VERSION` (6). Other libraries keep their older number. Version 5 is kept for the drawn cutter of PR #3906 (`CUTTER_VERSION`). The reader accepts 1 to 4 and 6. The PR that merges second adds the other number to the accepted list.

The decisions are in `docs/decisions/3368-taper-tip-form.md`.

## Breaking change

This PR changes the project file format in a way that older builds cannot read. The fix commit `ee24e1c73` has the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

- A project that holds a flat or ball taper tip is written as `.camproj` version 79. Older CamCraft builds refuse that file.
- A project with only sharp tips stays version 78. Older builds open it as before.
- A tool library with a flat or ball tip is written as `.camtools` version 6.
- The version guard stays. An older build must refuse the tip, because it reads a flat or ball tip as sharp, and a toolpath for that smaller tool can gouge.

## Review fix (finding 1 of the first review)

- A flat or ball taper with a short flute (the flute ends on the cone, under the full diameter) now ends its meridian with the radial shoulder at the flute top. `Tool::profile` draws the same shoulder, so the two agree. Commit `ee24e1c73`, `crates/tools/src/taper.rs` (`meridian_points`).
- Before the fix: a 6 mm taper, 90 degrees, 1 mm flat tip, 1 mm flute had a meridian that ended at r = 1.5 mm. The profile ended at r = 3 mm. A ball tip R0.5 with the same numbers ended at r = 1.2071 mm.
- The drawn profile (`taper::outline`) already had the shoulder. No other code builds the tip geometry.
- A sharp taper does not change. `meridian::tests::a_sharp_taper_keeps_its_profile_and_digest` passes.

## Readings

- Flat tip, 10 mm, 60 degrees, tip 4 mm, corner 0.5 mm: `r_flat` = 1.711 mm, the tangent point is on the cone line `r = r0 + z tan(30)`, and the cone meets the 5 mm radius at z = 5.196 mm.
- Ball tip, R0.5, 1 degree a side: the tangent point is on the ball and on the cone (both to 1e-9).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-tools` lib: `taper::tests::short_flat_profile_and_meridian_agree` and `taper::tests::short_ball_profile_and_meridian_agree` (review fix; red before the fix with the reviewer's numbers, green after). `meridian::tests::a_flat_and_a_ball_taper_meridian_agrees_with_the_profile` has the two short-flute tools too (it also builds their solid atoms).
- `camcraft-tools` lib: `taper::tests::*` (11 tests: the tip math, the named refusals, the profile, the meridian, the catalog tools, the words).
- `camcraft-tools` lib: `meridian::tests::a_sharp_taper_keeps_its_profile_and_digest` (every shipped sharp taper and one with an inert corner radius, against the profile code before this PR), `meridian::tests::a_flat_and_a_ball_taper_meridian_agrees_with_the_profile`.
- `crates/app/tests/tool_law.rs`: `every_operation_refuses_a_non_sharp_taper_by_name`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_deburr.rs`: `a_deburr_refuses_its_tool_after_a_flat_tip_edit` (the generation door).
- `crates/app/tests/tool_library.rs`: `a_tip_form_round_trips_and_steps_the_version`.
- `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`: `a_tip_form_round_trips_and_steps_the_project_version`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_edit_tool.rs`: `edit_tool_sets_the_tip_form` (also `set_tool_cutter_params`).
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `tool_library_editor::the_tip_form_row_shows_for_a_taper`, `tool_taper_tip_row::tests::*`.

## Gate (macOS, final head ee24e1c73)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: **117 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled** (18.0 min). This includes `tools suites: lib`, `app suites: example_catalog*`, `app suites: golden_cl` and `ui suites: lib`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main`: no conflict.
- Env: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`. No heavy step (P4).

## Earlier gate (Windows, winbuild, head 597460ab3)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: **117 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled** (24.4 min). The plan expected 40 to 60. The Tool struct literals in test helpers of `motion::drilling` and the `catalog.json` change pull the drilling suites and `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work` (all green). It does not go to the full batch.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed (on 40c28a009; the later commits change only app test files).
- The first gate run had 2 red steps (a missed future-version test in `pocket_no_adaptive.rs`, and a combo query in the new UI test). Both are fixed; the second run is green.
- Env: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`. No heavy step (P4).
- The tests were written first (commit edaba30e5). They were red by compile (the fields did not exist); they were not run red.

## Not exercised

- No generator, stock simulation or collision law reads a flat or ball tip yet. Each operation refuses such a tool by name. The consumer sub-issues of #3351 open those doors (#3370, #3371, #3373).
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row for `set_tool_cutter_params` (a process file) does not list the two new params. The tool description and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` do.
- The setup sheet and the tool table exports do not show the tip form.

## Screenshots (rendered headlessly with egui_kittest on Windows)

| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3368/before-chamfer-mill.png) | ![sharp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3368/after-sharp.png) |

| After: flat tip (Tip diameter row) | After: ball tip (radius in Corner radius) |

## Goldens moved

title: fix(ai): show key rejected after a provider authentication failure
body:
﻿## What changed

The provider Test control now shows a distinct "key rejected" status when a
cloud provider rejects the key, instead of one shared failure text.

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/settings_text.rs`: a new `is_auth_failure`
  rule classifies the authentication failure before the generic status match.
  The rule is:
  - HTTP 401 or 403: authentication failure, for every cloud provider behind
    Test (Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini).
  - Any other status: key rejected only when the provider error carries one of
    its documented classified auth fields: `authentication_error` (Anthropic
    `error.type`), `invalid_api_key` (OpenAI `error.code`), `api_key_invalid`
    or `UNAUTHENTICATED` (Gemini `error.status`), or Gemini's documented plain
    message "API key not valid". Gemini answers a bad key with HTTP 400, not
    401; without this shape Gemini would show the generic request failure.
  - The status line reads `Test failed: the key was rejected (HTTP <code>).`
    The provider response text is never shown beyond the already redacted
    classified fields, and the key is removed before any of this runs
    (`http.rs` redacts before truncation, unchanged).
- Other failures keep their own statuses, distinct from key rejected: wrong
  model (404 or 400/422 without an auth marker), billing or credits (402 or a
  billing marker), rate limit (429), provider outage (5xx), network, and an
  invalid Model name.
- `crates/app/tests/ai_http_review.rs`: pin that each provider's transport
  surfaces the HTTP authentication status and never the key.

## Classification note (conservative cases)

HTTP 403 can also mean a permission or region denial, not a bad key. The rule
still reports key rejected for 403: the hint ("paste a new key") names the
most common cause, and no provider here returns 403 for a credit or model
failure. A 400 is only key rejected through the documented marker, never
guessed, so a wrong model on Gemini stays a model failure.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::settings_failure_details::authentication_failure_shows_key_rejected_for_each_cloud_provider`
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::settings_failure_details::gemini_bad_request_with_documented_key_error_shows_key_rejected`
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::settings_failure_details::non_auth_cloud_test_failures_remain_distinct_from_key_rejected`
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::settings_hand_test::failed_test_names_the_cause_the_model_and_what_to_try` (updated wording)
- `authentication_failure_surfaces_the_http_status_for_each_cloud_provider` (`camcraft-app`, `ai_http_review`)

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test ai_http_review`: 7 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 307 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1612 passed, 8 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

The live-ai lane (#3803) does not exist yet. Its wrong-key step ("Use a wrong
key and confirm the key rejected status") is already specified there and was
not run here; every pin above runs over loopback HTTP fixtures, not real
credentials or remote services. The Gemini 400 marker path is pinned from the
published API error shape, not from a live provider answer.

Changelog: AI Chat: the provider Test shows a key rejected status after an authentication failure, with other causes kept distinct.

Fixes #3804

title: feat(ui): add, move and remove the axes of a machine in the file editor
body:
The Machines pane's file editor gets an "Axis chain" group. The group adds, moves and removes the axis parts of a `.mch` file, reverses a linear axis, and sets the direction of a rotary axis. The editor changes the file's own JSON, so it keeps every key that it does not know. The decisions and the open questions are in `docs/decisions/2756-machine-axis-chain.md`.

**Before** (v0.26.0): the file editor of the same grblHAL 3-axis machine, with no Axis chain group above General.

![Before: the Machines file editor in v0.26.0, General first and no Axis chain group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2756/axis-chain-before.png)

**After** (this PR): the Axis chain group above General.

![After: the Axis chain group on the same 3-axis mill, above General](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2756/axis-chain.png)

## What changed

- **`MachineDraft`** (`crates/app/src/machine/chain.rs`, `draft.rs`) adds, moves and removes axis parts in `kinematics.default.parts`, like `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant`. A refused edit changes nothing. The validator judges the result as before.
  - A new axis goes **on the table** (beside the table's axes, before the head; a rotary there turns the work) or **carries the head** (it takes the head's slot; a rotary there tilts the tool).
  - **Remove** keeps what the axis carried: its `parts` take its place, in order. Its controller row goes with it.
  - **Up and Down** trade an axis with its neighbour row. The tree keeps its shape, so a move never changes which slot carries the head. An axis keeps all its own keys (`pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover`, `sign_convention`, unknown keys) and gets the `parent` and `chain_order` (#1962) of its new slot.
  - A move trades only with an axis of the same kind (rotary or linear) that moves the same thing (the work or the tool). Other moves are refused, and the refusal says to remove the axis and add it again.
  - A linear is reversed with `"direction": -1` (#373). Back to standard removes the key.
  - A rotary's `axis` is ±X, ±Y, ±Z or three numbers. The editor suggests the RS-274 letter (about X is A, about Y is B, about Z is C) and adds a note to a row whose letter does not agree. It does not refuse it.
- **The validator** keys the work-length refusals by axis and key (`A nose_to_axis`, `work_length_refusals` in `crates/post/src/machine/swing.rs`), so each refusal shows at its row and not above the grid. The rule is the parser's own rule.
- **The editor rows** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/machine_axis_chain.rs`) draw in one property grid, like General and the editor's other groups (`prop_grid` in `layout/form.rs`, #1122): one setting per row, the label in the first column and the control beside it, help as a hover text. A first version pushed the controls to the right edge (`prop_row`), so in a wide pane they drifted away from their labels. Each axis has a row with its letter and kind and the buttons Up, Down and ✖. Their accessible names are "Move A up", "Move A down" and "Remove A". The direction and the place of a new axis are dropdowns.
  - `nose_to_axis` (#804) and `axis_to_table` (#1107) are rows for a rotary that turns the work. A rotary that carries the head shows them only when the file states one, so that the user can clear it.
  - A row whose `offset` has no parent rotary gets a note (see Q1 below).
  - The fields have stable ids, so a note or a refusal that comes or goes above a field does not take the focus while the user types.
- **The rows are built once per edit** (the frame-cost rule, #2238). `MachineDraft::chain_view` (`crates/app/src/machine/chain_view.rs`) holds the rows, each row's notes and the refusal keys that show at a row. title: fix(contour): enter every wall-side ring by the ramp, not the pass link plunge
body:
Stacked on #3834 (merge #3834 first).

## What changed

- `contour_link::ring_entry` now applies on the wall side too. On the wall side it applies to the Ramp and Helix arms only.
- `contour::emit_band` calls `ring_entry` for each untabbed ring after the first ring of a level, inside or outside.
- An outside ring after another ring now goes through `engage_level`. It takes the wall-side ramp of #3833 (`contour_wall_ramp`).
- The helix stands down to that ramp. It says so in its one existing note.
- The traverse between the parts rides the pass link plane (`Step::traverse` from #3834). Pass `Clearance` crosses at `clearance_z`. Pass `Retract` crosses at the hop plane.
- These stay as before:
  - the wall-side Arc entry (its own hop and wall arc);
  - tabbed levels;
  - the Plunge entry;
  - a `KeepDown` pass link that holds its proof (it feeds straight across);
  - a ring that is too short for the ramp angle (it grazes, with the existing "too short" note).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3917-contour-outside-ring-entry.md`.

## Cause

`ring_entry` returned `None` on the wall side. Thus each ring after the first ring at a level took `ring_link`. That link lifts, crosses and plunges straight down at the plunge feed. It posts no note.

## Readings

The pin uses the `outside_ramped` fixture: tool 10 mm, stepdown 1 mm, 3 levels, bottom Z -3, ramp 5 degrees, 16 mm square parts 40 mm apart.

| Entry | 2 parts (before / after) | 3 parts (before / after) |
|---|---|---|
| Ramp 5 deg, axial dives | 3 / 0 | 6 / 0 |
| Plunge, axial dives | 6 / 6 | 9 / 9 |

Before the fix, the notes were empty (`[]`).

## Tests

- Pin: `every_outside_ring_of_several_parts_is_entered_by_the_wall_side_ramp` (`camcraft-motion`, `tests/machining2d.rs`).
  - It covers 2 and 3 parts, Ramp and Helix, and pass `Clearance` and pass `Retract`.
  - It asserts: no axial dive, no `Plunge` move, the steepest descent is at most 5 degrees, and each ring-to-ring crossing rides the pass link plane.
- Red before the fix: yes. On the #3834 head the pin fails: `2 parts, Ramp, pass Clearance: no ring dives: []`, left 3, right 0.
- Mutation: I put back `ring_to_ring && inside && !tabbed` at the call site. The pin fails with the same message. I restored the fix. The pin passes.

title: feat(tools): add metric tap-drill and clearance drills, a 3 mm ball and a 6 mm bull nose to the catalog
body:
## What changed

The starter tool catalog (`assets/tools/catalog.json`) gets 16 tools:

- `BN-0300`: a 3 mm ball end mill.
- `BB-0600-R1`: a 6 mm bull nose end mill with a 1 mm corner radius.
- 14 jobber drills: a tap drill and a clearance drill (ISO 273 medium) for each coarse thread from M3 to M12.

| Thread | Tap drill | Clearance drill |
|---|---|---|
| M3 | `DR-0250` | `DR-0340` |
| M4 | `DR-0330` | `DR-0450` |
| M5 | `DR-0420` | `DR-0550` |
| M6 | `DR-0500` | `DR-0660` |
| M8 | `DR-0680` | `DR-0900` |
| M10 | `DR-0850` | `DR-1100` |
| M12 | `DR-1020` | `DR-1350` |

Each new tool goes into its family in diameter order. The other tools keep their order.

The cutting data follows the rules of the catalog's own rows. Below 6 mm, the drill rpm and feed are interpolated between `DR-0200`, `DR-0300`, `DR-0400` and `DR-0600`. Thus a larger drill never turns faster than a smaller drill. From 6 mm up, the drills use the cutting speed and the feed per revolution of `DR-0600`. `docs/decisions/3036-metric-catalog.md` gives each rule and its source.

The drill flute length is 3 x D on a 0.5 mm step. A length such as 9.9 mm made `spun::tests::a_parametric_holder_stacks_bit_identically_to_the_cylinder` fail: the spun holder band length was 35.00000000000001 and the cylinder was 35.0. A length on a 0.5 mm step is exact in binary. This PR does not change the spun holder code.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick`: green (`tools suites: lib`, `app suites: mcp`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: fix(motion): warn on start-side stand-in entries and a Plunge into stock
body:
**Update at 6e381cc81 (review rework):** A selected Arc on an Outside ring pass with no air room is now refused by name (`OUTSIDE_AIR_REFUSAL`). The op posts no ramp stand-in. The pins are now `outside_pocket_arc_without_air_is_refused` and `outside_pocket_selected_entry_keeps_one_warning`. The PR comment 7136819007 has the details and the gate results. Where the text below says that Arc keeps a ramp stand-in on Outside, this update replaces it.

## What changed

A plain 2D Pocket with "Pass starts at: Outside" and no stock known has no air room (#3746). Before this change, two entries were notes only:

- With Arc, a later pass start in material took a ramp along the pass (`descent_dive::entry_restart`).
- With Plunge, the pass link plunged into uncut stock with no note.

`entry_status_lines` dropped the notes, and no warning was posted.

Now, on a start-side ladder (`Motion::cleared_links`, the #3316 link law):

- Each named stand-in entry (a ramp, a helix, an axial dive or a plunge) writes the marker `ENTRY_STAND_IN_NOTE`. The op posts one advisory `Warning::EntryStandIn { at, entries }` that counts the stand-ins.
- A pass link that plunges into a pass start in material writes `PLUNGE_INTO_STOCK_NOTE`. The op posts one advisory `Warning::PlungeIntoStock`. If the op already posts `EntryNotRecommended` for the selected Plunge, it does not post this second warning. Thus the plunge is named once.
- `entry_status_lines` shows each stand-in note as a `warning: Entry: ... - fix: ...` line. The two marker notes add no line, because the op warning is already in the status area.
- MCP names the new kinds `entry_stand_in` and `plunge_into_stock`.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3884-start-side-entry-warnings.md`. Arc with no air room keeps a safe, named stand-in with a Warning. It does not refuse, because a refusal would refuse every plain Outside pocket that uses the default Arc and has no stock.

The new code is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/entry_warn.rs`. The changes to `generate.rs` and `types.rs` add only a few lines each. Both files were already over 400 lines.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_engagement::outside_pocket_arc_ramp_is_a_warning` (pin 1): the band pocket with no stock and Arc has named stand-ins, and has exactly one `EntryStandIn` warning that counts them.
- `pass_start_engagement::outside_pocket_plunge_into_stock_is_one_warning` (pin 2): the same pocket with Plunge has more than one plunge, and has exactly one warning that names the plunge.
- `camcraft-ui` lib `approach_page::top_stock_tests::each_stand_in_entry_is_a_warning_line` (pin 3): the four stand-in note forms from the review are warning lines.

Red first: the pins use the new API (`entry_warnings`, `entry_stand_ins`, the marker notes), so they do not compile on `main`. Without the API, main has no warning and no status line for these notes. The review of #3872 proved this with a probe.

## Gates

- Targeted pins: green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 324 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (76.7 min); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Heavy steps (P1 under the safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: offset_pass_start"` ok (1146 s); `--only "app heavy: pocket_pass_start"` ok (10 s).

## Not exercised

- No app-level test that reads the op warnings for this pocket. The op adds the result of `entry_warnings` with one line in `generate.rs`.
- The stand-ins of Auto ladders show as warning lines on the op page, but they post no op warning (out of scope; see the decision).

Changelog: A 2D Pocket with "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside now posts a warning for each entry that is not the selected one, and for a selected Plunge that plunges into uncut stock. Before, these were notes only.

title: fix(motion): stop inter-level rapid at feed height above prior floor in 3D Pocket
body:
## What changed

This change ensures that rapids between levels and on pass restarts in 3D Pocket stop at feed height above the last cut floor instead of reaching the floor with zero margin (#3671):
- Added `restart: bool` to `Ask` in `camcraft_motion::machining3d::descent` and `ladder.rs`:
  - On level transitions (`restart = false`): the descent starting plane `from(lvl, a, ramp)` adds `ap.plunge_height` (the operation's feed height) to `mat_top(lvl, a)`, capped under traverse plane `lvl.tz`. Rapids stop at feed height above the prior floor; the entire descent into the next level is fed (e.g. helical feed or linear ramp).
  - On pass restarts (`restart = true`): the descent plane stays on `a.prev_z` (`mat_top`) to prevent ramp depth inflation. Rapids stop at `rapid_z = (zf + ap.plunge_height).min(lvl.tz)` and feed down vertically before entering the ramp or helix moves (`push_helix`, `push_zig3`, and the diagonal ramp arm).
- Regenerated example catalog case `3d/rough-finish` (`rough-finish.camproj` and `rough-finish.nc`).
- Updated bitwise golden digest for `rotary_adaptive::offset_rings_on_the_wrap_are_the_program_they_always_were`.
- Added pinning test `interlevel_rapid_stops_at_feed_height_above_prior_floor` in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_3d_rough_finish.rs`.
- Updated decision record `docs/decisions/3671-3d-pocket-interlevel-rapid-margin.md`.

## Goldens moved

- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc` and `.camproj`: 77 rapids stop 2 mm higher (6 inter-level entries and 71 pass restarts). 71 new vertical plunge moves feed down to the cut plane.
- `crates/motion/tests/rotary_adaptive.rs`: `GOLDEN_RINGS` digest moves from `(2363, 10_359_925_331_182_573_356)` to `(2387, 3_362_882_240_517_259_677)` (24 additional feed-down moves) due to the same feed height clearance margin on the rotary wrap program.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask catalog --case 3d/rough-finish` ran cleanly and updated the project and NC program.
- In `rough-finish.nc`, all rapid moves between levels now stop with a 2.0 mm margin above the previous cut floor.
- All 5 test cases in `catalog_3d_rough_finish` pass.

title: fix(ui): show key rejected on provider authentication failure
body:
## What changed

AI Chat classifies cloud provider authentication failures and displays a safe key rejected status.

- Classify provider authentication failures (`is_auth_failure`) across all cloud providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini).
- Handle Google Gemini authentication failure responses (HTTP 400 with `API_KEY_INVALID` or `API key not valid`, and HTTP 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`) as key rejected instead of a generic model error.
- Guard against echoed model names: model names are never treated as authentication evidence, and explicit model refusals remain distinct.
- Keep non-authentication failures (HTTP 404 model not found, HTTP 402 billing, HTTP 429 rate limit, HTTP 500 server unavailable, and network unreachable) distinct from authentication failures.
- Redact secrets so that raw secret keys and unredacted provider payloads are never exposed.

## Screenshots

Before: Gemini HTTP 400 displays that the provider refused the request or the model name.

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JSwetz/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3845/before.png)

After: Gemini HTTP 400 displays that the provider rejected the key and advises setting a new key.

![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JSwetz/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3845/after.png)

- `anthropic_cloud_test_authentication_failure_shows_key_rejected`: loopback test pins that Anthropic HTTP 401 shows key rejected and redacts secrets.
- `gemini_cloud_test_bad_request_auth_failure_shows_key_rejected`: loopback test pins that Gemini HTTP 400 `API_KEY_INVALID` shows key rejected.
- `gemini_cloud_test_forbidden_auth_failure_shows_key_rejected`: loopback test pins that Gemini HTTP 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` shows key rejected.

title: feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal
body:
feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal

## What changed

Issue #2772, parts 1 and 2 of the plan in
`docs/decisions/2772-rotary-4axis-refusal.md`. The rotary kinds
(Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) read their rotation
axis from a STATEMENT first; today's free fit is the fallback, and
nothing stated keeps every behaviour bit for bit.

1. The stated-axis resolver, `camcraft_app::rotary_stated` over
   `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_stated`:
   - the op's own `stated_axis` direction first, else the mounted
     machine's stated rotary lines (a stated `axis` vector, else the
     RS-274 letter's line - the index-swing clause's own
     `rotary_line` reading, so one law reads both doors);
   - each line anchored through the setup's work offset origin (the
     indexed post's setup law: the WCS sits on the rotary
     centreline), canonicalized the fit's own way (signed, pinned to
     the `o . u = 0` foot), so a part truly on the line keeps the
     fitted path move for move;
   - JUDGED, never trusted: the fit's own concurrency share,
     coarseness skip and bearing law about the stated line
     (`axis_stated::judged_any`). A disagreement refuses by name:
     the part's own fitted axis and the two acts that fix it when
     the model is a revolve placed off the line; the freeform's
     4-axis wording (with the pinned "share no rotation axis"
     words) when no axis fits at all. Never a silent fall back to a
     free fit when a line was stated. A stated line that leans or is
     no direction refuses by name, as the swing clause does.
2. The caller switch, stated first / fit fallback:
   - `fixture::rotary_axis_of` - feeds the sim's chord pass
     (`stock_sim_rotary::rotary_plan`), the first traverse and the
     post gate's struck-steel law (`fixture_struck`): all three
     follow with no change of their own;
   - `first_traverse::turned_axis` - already prefers the job axis,
     which is now the stated-or-fitted line;
   - `rotary_law::rotary_into` - the radial field verdict takes the
     job's resolved axis (`rotary_axis`), keeping its fail-closed
     Gouge for the nothing-known case;
   - `rotary_picks::usable` and the centre-cutting audit's
     `revolved_bar_stated` - judge and read the resolved axis;
   - the letter door `rotary_gate::letter_gate` (moved from
     generate.rs) - a stated line answers the letter without a fit,
     held to the machine inventory;
   - the three motion kernels grow `*_stated` entries
     (`rotary_contour_stated`, `rotary_parallel_over_stated`,
     `rotary_offset_stated`) that take the judged axis; the plain
     entries keep the fit inside, so turning, drilling and every
     existing golden path are untouched.
3. The op param: `stated_axis` on the three arms - a direction
   ratio, never unit-scaled (the machine file's own law for its
   `axis` vector), through the WCS origin, overriding the machine
   line. UI edit (the rotary page's Passes tab, an armed group of
   three direction numbers riding the existing EditOperationParams
   commit), MCP patch (`edit_operation`'s merge patch over the DTO,
   automatic), project round-trip (`stated_axis`, PROJECT_VERSION
   steps to v81 - BREAKING, an incompatible project-format change.
   v78 is upstream's own step (eserved_tools, #2604), v79 its
   conditional tip form (#3368) and v80 the minimum_cone_radius step
   (#3153); a v78 or v79 reader accepts this branch's old v78 and
   drops the stated key on re-save. v81 is the next correctly-ordered
   free version: an older reader refuses the file rather than drop
   the statement and turn the part about an axis the user never
   named. A v78, v79 and v80 file still open - the v79 keys read
   natively, pinned by the round-trip test).
4. The cache stamp: the op's own direction, the machine's stated
   lines and the WCS anchor enter the digest ONLY when a line is
   stated - no cached path of a document without one goes stale.

## The readings

- The WCS origin is the stated line's anchor: the post subtracts the
  work offset from world coordinates, so in program coordinates the
  rotary centreline passes through the WCS origin - the same law the
  index-swing clause and the lathe spindle law read.
- The judge is the fit's own (`axis.rs`'s `data_of` + `judge`): the
  tolerance, the 90% concurrency share, the coarseness skip and the
  bearing law, evaluated about the stated line instead of a candidate
  from the eigen search. On the reporter's helical rotor the judge
  fails and the radial raster stays LOCKED (the decision doc's law:
  its radial pose can gouge on helical lobes) - the disagreement
  refusal says so and names the 4-axis case.
- A machine whose work-turning rotary states no `axis` vector keeps
  today's fit (absent is not stated, never zero). A trunnion's
  work-turning pair is read in chain order and the first line the
  model holds wins, so a standing revolve takes the C and a lying
  one takes the A.

## Pinning tests

- motion `axis_stated_tests`: a revolve holds its stated line and
  reads the fitted axis bit for bit; the canonical line is signed
  and pinned; a stated line away from the part names the part's own
  axis; the helical screw refuses with the 4-axis wording; an empty
  mesh refuses like the fit.
- app `rotary_stated_axis`:
  `a_stated_machine_line_generates_the_fitted_path` (microARC 4 +
  laid revolve: move-for-move the fitted program),
  `the_millturns_stated_c_carries_the_standing_bar` (C answered
  without a fit, the stamp runs),
  `the_screw_rotor_on_a_stated_A_is_refused_by_name` (the radial
  kinds stay locked on the screw),
  `the_screw_rotor_without_a_stated_line_keeps_the_old_refusal`
  (the pinned "share no rotation axis" words untouched),
  `a_stated_line_away_from_the_part_names_the_parts_own_axis` (both
  the disagreement and the letter-door wordings),
  `a_stated_line_the_part_holds_on_a_machine_that_has_it_generates`
  (the op's own statement, either sign),
  `a_work_offset_move_moves_the_stated_line_and_refuses` (the
  anchor is the WCS's own position),
  `a_stated_axis_round_trips_the_project_file` (v81 round-trip, v77 steps up unstated),
  `a_v77_file_opens_and_a_newer_file_is_refused` (the version pin),
  `a_stated_axis_on_every_rotary_kind_needs_the_new_reader` (the
  old-reader boundary, one op of each rotary kind),
  `a_common_translation_does_not_defeat_the_stated_line_judge` (the
  review's mutation: the model and stock at Y+10000, clearance 100 -
  the work offset on the part generates, 1 mm and 2 mm off refuse by
  name).
- motion `axis_stated_tests`, the translation pins: a part moved with
  its line holds it on every coordinate axis and reads the fit's own
  axis; a wrong line 1 mm off on each of the three coordinate planes
  refuses at home and after every common translation.
- app `project_roundtrip`:
  `a_tip_form_round_trips_and_steps_the_project_version` (the ladder
  stepped past v79: a tip-form file writes v81, and a v79 file - the
  tip-form era's own - still opens and reads its tips whole).
- ui `egui_app::tests::rotary_stated_axis` (new, the review's item):
  the group's labels, roles and enabled state, the Apply commit and
  one undo, across the three rotary kinds
  (`the_stated_axis_group_arms_edits_and_undoes_on_every_rotary_kind`);
  the help text follows the resolver's order - the machine's stated
  line first, the fit only when nothing is stated
  (`the_help_text_follows_the_resolver_machine_line_first`).
- Test placement: `crates/app/tests/rotary_stated_axis.rs` stays a
  top-level binary because no existing directory suite covers the
  rotary domain - its siblings (`rotary_verify.rs`,
  `rotary_letter.rs`, `rotary_contour_x.rs`) are all top-level - and
  its gate map spans app::rotary_stated, app::operation, app::project
  and the motion judge.
- app `rotary_gate`: `a_stated_line_answers_the_letter_without_a_fit`
  (the screw's fit refuses, the stated line still answers).
- app `rotary_field_parity`:
  `the_stated_axis_parallel_reads_the_radial_law` - the heavy-lane
  parity of the stated-A program (the field eye vs the radial law,
  `#[ignore]`d like its three siblings; the quick suite pins the
  path equality, this lane proves the stated axis flows the whole
  sim pipeline at the verdict class).
- The continuous 4-axis example regenerated at v81 (its op follows
  the microARC's stated line - the same path the fit reads).

## What was NOT exercised

- The heavy parity lane runs at a cut, not here (the quick gate
  pins the path equality instead).
- No UI pixel snapshot is touched (release-lane only).

## Screenshots

Before and after of the Passes tab's stated-axis controls (the
fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, captured through the
egui_kittest properties-page harness - no pixels enter this branch):

- [before](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-before.png) -
  the pre-change Passes tab, no stated-axis group
- [after, unstated](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-after-unstated.png) -

- [after, stated](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-after-stated.png) -

- [after, the offset kind](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-offset-after-stated.png) -
  the same group on Rotary Offset's Passes tab

- The RADIAL DROP FINISH KERNEL and the radial-step roughing

  `mkinney:issue/2772-radial-drop` holds that work. This PR's

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- Skims on an open run are not judged per pass by the wire verify (it
  refuses them by name); a follow-up can split the passes and judge
  each at its own kerf.
- Taper, burnout and 4-axis cuts do not read the overlap; each refuses
  an open run or walks the closed lap as before.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
  included.
- Three steps are red, each not caused by this change:
  - `app suites: docs_troubleshooting` - the stem of a clearance
    message spans a line-continued string in `crates/sim/src/verify`;
    no file of this change is in its sources.
  - `app suites: example_catalog` (2d/drill-overfeed) - the fixture
    `refusal.txt` on disk reads CRLF against the generated LF; a
    checkout line-ending state, no fixture touched here.
  - `ui suites: lib` - a native STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION at 20 test
    threads after all tests printed ok; it re-runs green in full
    (`1431 passed; 0 failed`) and at 1 and 4 threads. A teardown race
    of the headless window harness on this machine, not this change.

Changelog: Wire Contour: a stated closing overlap rides the cut past its seam; a centre-line slit side for open runs; skim passes on open runs re-entered from the air.

title: fix(multiaxis): rotate the rotaries before the first five-axis approach descent
body:
﻿## What changed

Five-axis generators set the first station's pose on the modal builder
and then pushed the descend to first contact, so the rotary swing rode
the approach move: the machine turned the A/C head while the tool
descended, and the ball swept through unknown air and through the rim
it approached.

The fix splits the approach. The pose is stated as its own zero-travel
Rapid (a standstill rotary index - the tip held on the hop plane, or at
the tip the machine already holds), and the Plunge/cut descends under
the pose already stated:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve.rs` (`contour_curve`): every
  chain's approach swings first, then plunges.
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs` (the stamp emit loop, all
  posed kinds - parallel5d, flow5d, swarf5d, rough, contour5d): at
  every rapid-to-cut re-entry where the pose changes, the swing is
  emitted at a standstill before the cut. Intermediate cut moves keep
  the modal tilt law unchanged.

No new `MoveKind`. The builder already keeps a zero-travel move whose
pose changed (it drops one only when the tip AND the pose both stand),
and the post already solves a zero-travel segment as a pure rotary
reorientation (`ds_tip == 0` in `crates/post/src/post/g93.rs`), so the
swing always commands. That is the answer to the zero-travel question:
the swing is a zero-travel rapid, not a short travel move - a travel
move would drag the tip sideways while the head turns, and a dropped
zero-travel move cannot occur, because a drop needs the pose to match
the held one, in which case no rotation is due.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 28 steps, 0 failed
  (motion lib 536 passed, multiaxis, multiaxis_avoid, multiaxis_rough,
  pivot5d, swarf_pose_continuity, app operations, posed_contact and the
  rest all green).
- The existing laws were amended where the swing touches them, each in
  its own terms: a TRAVEL rapid still inherits its pose
  (`rapids_hold_the_pose_they_inherit`, `rapid_pose_contract` - the
  zero-travel index is the second legal way a rapid states a pose,
  beside the swarf link's ball-centred swing); the air-link ratchet
  counts travel links only; the pivot-law ball readers skip the
  swing (it cuts nothing) through `no_swings`/`sans_swings` helpers.
- A decision record sits in `docs/decisions/3414-approach-rotary-order.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `the_approach_rotates_before_it_descends` (crates/motion/tests/pivot5d.rs):
  a zero-travel rotary swing precedes the first descend; the plunge
  holds the pose the swing stated; no pose change rides any move that
  crosses from air to material, over contour_curve, parallel5d, flow5d
  and swarf5d.

## What was not exercised

- No posted G-code golden was regenerated (the post's pure-rotary path
  is covered by its own suite; the swing was not posted end to end on
  a real machine file).
- The heavy lanes were not run; the diff touches `camcraft-motion`, so
  the release-tier lane check stays with the review/cut.

New test binary reason: `crates/app/tests/approach_rotary_order.rs` pins, at the app level, that the five-axis approach rotates the machine to the first pose before the tool descends; no existing app suite covers the approach ordering across rotary words, so the pin takes a binary of its own.

## Changelog

Five-axis approach moves rotate the machine to the first pose before
the tool descends to the part, no longer while it descends.

title: feat(chamfer): select a tip offset
body:
## What changed

2D Chamfer has a `Tip offset` setting. A positive offset moves the cone axis toward physical air and lowers its virtual tip by `(tip offset + chamfer width) * tan(angle)`. The selected cone band runs from the tip offset to the tip offset plus chamfer width. The declared `EdgeBreak` stays on the original selected edge with the authored width and depth.

Closed loops and selected open chains support the setting. Generation refuses a wrong Side, material crossing, excessive tool radius or flute reach, and an offset that folds or loses any selected boundary span. The partial-collapse refusal covers a narrow branch disappearing while its parent loop survives. Zero offset preserves the complete legacy closed and open `Toolpath`, including floating-point depth bytes.

The parameter reaches the UI, commands, stamps, project files, and MCP create/edit/read/save/reset. The UI shows the control and derived virtual-tip height. The persisted field remains `minimum_cone_radius`.

## Breaking project-format change

Project format **v79** cannot be opened by v78 readers. The fix commit records the existing format break with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Migration preserves the legacy zero offset; project round trips preserve positive values.

## Review fixes

1. Check every original boundary span after a positive offset; loop count alone is insufficient.
2. Restore the exact legacy depth calculation on both zero-offset routes. Compare complete results with captured pre-feature paths.
3. Add before/after control and height-note screenshots below.
4. Record the reason for each retained test binary below.
5. Record the format break and correct the body to v79.

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
  - A helix inside the uncut core of a tool that is not centre-cutting (review finding on 4bd091166). The core is `plunge_law::CORE` of the tool radius. The wall circle must stand at least that far off the hole axis (`rc >= CORE * r`). The message names the helix radius, the uncut core and the smallest hole that the tool helixes (Ø9 for a Ø6 tool with no leave). A centre-cutting tool keeps the small helix.
- Pass starts at (#3360, from `main`) on a Helical Bore: one helix for each hole has no ring order. Inside and Outside are refused by name at the command (`sane.rs`) and in the generator (`bore_started`). The Passes tab shows the refusal under the row. Auto is unchanged.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and a Lead-in hint that the level links do not apply.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
  - `a_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_of_a_non_centre_cutting_tool_is_refused`: the review's case (Ø6.5, Ø6 tool, 0.4 mm per turn, helix radius 0.25 mm). The NC tool is refused with "1.500 mm uncut core" and "9.000 mm". Ø9 and the issue's Ø11 counterbore still helix with that tool.
  - `a_helical_bore_refuses_a_pass_order_by_name`.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `a_small_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_is_refused_through_the_operation`: the review's probe through `operation::generate`. The NC tool is refused; the CC tool keeps the small helix with no plunge.
  - `a_helical_bore_with_a_pass_order_is_refused_by_name`: the command and the generator both refuse it.
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch.
- `egui_app::tests::pass_start::a_helical_bore_says_the_pass_start_refusal` (ui lib): Rings take the order; Helical shows the refusal line.

## Gates

All gates ran on the final head 6932f4022. This head adds the core fix (c85bdd982) and merges `upstream/main` four times, the last at 33597a2fb. Each conflict was resolved by keeping the two sides:

- d5fafe8be (main at 6cfc0a6d4): #3360 added Pass starts at to Bore. The Bore records, the project file, the stamp, the params patch, the generator and the Passes tab now carry both `strategy` and `pass_start` (13 files; `git show --remerge-diff d5fafe8be`). The three Bore test literals get the other field.
- 7ae8b1532 (main at 01e177bf5): two mod lines in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`.
- 88f7fc420 (main at 81365c33b): two new tests side by side in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/pass_start.rs` (main's #3745 test and the helical pass-start test).
- 6932f4022 (main at 33597a2fb): no conflict.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 809 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (108.3 min). It includes `motion suites: bore_helix`, `motion suites: bore_pass_start`, `app suites: bore_helical`, `app suites: bore_pass_start` and `ui suites: lib`.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets` on `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean (on the merge 88f7fc420; the last merge brought only main's commits and no conflict).
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 104 steps, 1 failed (63.6 min). The known-fail steps are red as expected.
  - The red step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. It fails at `pocket3d_hsm.rs:79`: the STEP mesh of `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` has 5232 facets, and the pin is 6228. This test is a 3D Pocket and does not use the Bore operation. `Cargo.lock`, `crates/kernel` and `testdata` are the same as `main`. #3886 reports this step red on `main`.
- An earlier quick gate on 88f7fc420 (merge of `main` at 81365c33b) had 809 steps and 1 failed step, `app suites: plunge_depth_tab`. That `main` had #3866 and #3679 without the re-pin of #3927. The merge of 33597a2fb brought #3927, and the step is green on the final head.

## Screenshots

The Bore operation page, rendered by the UI test harness (`egui_kittest`) from a real Bore operation.

| | Rings | Helical |
|---|---|---|
| Passes tab | ![Passes, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-rings.png) | ![Passes, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-helical.png) |
| Heights tab | ![Heights, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-rings.png) | ![Heights, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-helical.png) |

- Passes tab: the Strategy combo shows the two strategies. The Spring pass check shows only for Helical.
- Heights tab: the last Levels row is "Stepdown" for Rings and "Helix pitch" for Helical.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A tool that is not centre-cutting helixes only when the helix clears its uncut core. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.
- The screenshots show the head 4bd091166. The new refusal line under Pass starts at is pinned by the UI test, not by a screenshot.

Changelog: The Bore operation has a Helical strategy: one continuous helix on the wall radius to the floor, one floor circle, an optional spring pass, then a move to the centre. It cuts a counterbore or a hole up to twice the tool diameter without a plunge.

title: fix(post): name mixed wire conditions in a native wire EDM group
body:
Stacked on #2993. Review [the delta above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/fa31e7120ca8c1fdbeceaeec755884b87bb03644...7e3df82930c1275dae6f8108055ca42900bece99).

## What changed

This head merges #2993 (`fa31e7120`) into the PR branch. Main's rewrite of #2984 (`ee0dafe23`) replaced the old script writer (`crates/post/src/agie/jescript.rs`). Each conflict takes the frame side. Above the merge, one commit adds what main does not have yet:

- A group that mixes `AGIE_QN2` and `AGIE_BERCO_RA035` gets its own refusal, in either work order: `The works of a group must use the same wire condition. This group mixes AGIE_BERCO_RA035 and AGIE_QN2`. The check is in `crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs`, before the single-punch limit of CCB035. No job directory is written. Before this change, the frame refused the same group with the single-punch text, which did not name the mixed conditions. A group that requests `AGIE_BERCO_RA035` for every work still gets the single-punch text.
- The machine template `agiecut-classic-2s.mch` no longer tells the user to set X/Y travel endpoints. The native wire EDM post refuses a profile that states them.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/2984-agie-quality-binding.md`, with a section that lists what main already covers.

## What main already covers (dropped from this PR)

Each item was checked on `fa31e7120`:

- Zero working steps on import: `crates/post/src/agie_setup/piece.rs` writes one quality object for the piece and `ASDELETE` for each work. No `ASAGIE` (asserted in `crates/post/src/agie/tests.rs`, `group_tests.rs`, `quality_tests.rs`). The receipt reports `working_steps_generated: false` (`crates/app/src/script/report.rs:83`). From `ee0dafe23` and the stack ports.
- One requested quality for each piece, CCB030 or CCB035, with the receipt offsets and the user-guide TECCUT procedure (#2966 port, `agie_setup/quality.rs`, `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`).
- The repeat-import "new piece" text (user guide, line 164) and the refusal of a stated X or Y travel (`crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs`, test `generic_preview_inside_declared_travel_cannot_clear_native_offsets`).
- The smoothing skip of the native post (`crates/app/tests/smoothing.rs`, `posting::agie::is_native`), the plasma-stream refusal (`crates/app/tests/plasma_post_refusals.rs`) and the 11 recorded-stream refusal goldens (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/agie-native/*.refusal`). The frame text is "Native wire EDM job files require ...". The PR text was "Agie native wire EDM requires ...".
- The default-machine diagnostic (#3092, on main).

## Readings

- `a_group_with_mixed_wire_conditions_is_refused_in_either_order`: both orders exit non-zero with the exact text above, and `PAIR20` does not exist.
- No posted byte changes. The diff against `fa31e7120` touches no golden and no writer.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-app --test agie_native`: `quality::a_group_with_mixed_wire_conditions_is_refused_in_either_order` (new), and the existing `quality::ra035_refuses_a_group_an_arc_punch_a_die_and_a_cutoff`, `quality::the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality`.

## Not exercised

- No control import for this head. No job bytes change, so the control results of #2993 stay valid.
- No physical cut.
- No heavy step. The issue is `P6`.

## Gate

`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on `7e3df8293`: 1201 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 46.9 min. The plan included `post suites: script_agie_native` and `app suites: agie_native`. It also included `clippy -D warnings` with `--all-targets` on geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, gpu and ui.

`git merge-tree --write-tree 7e3df8293 origin/main` is clean.

Changelog: A native wire EDM group that mixes the AGIE_QN2 and AGIE_BERCO_RA035 conditions is refused with a message that names the two conditions.

## Goldens moved

Against current main, this PR adds two recorded programs. Both come from the parent #2993 (tangent-loop writer, `crates/post/src/agie/tangent_profile.rs`, export through `export_round_with_review`), which is in this PR's diff until #2993 merges. This PR's own delta above #2993 adds or changes no recorded program. No golden that is on main changes.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/ROUND20.ISO` (A): the `examples/agie/rounded-punch.camscript` job. A convex punch from one selected DXF chain of four straight lines and four tangent corner arcs (two arcs of radius 6 mm, two of radius 4 mm; centres (14,−8), (16,10), (−14,8), (−16,−10)), on 20 mm stock, quality CCB030. Nominal geometry with incremental I/J arc centres, counter-clockwise, entry from the waste side on a straight side, 1 mm separation.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/THREEARC.ISO` (A): the `examples/agie/three-corner-punch.camscript` job. A convex punch from three tangent arcs (centres (24,0), (0,18), (0,0)) joined by straight sides, one of them oblique, on 20 mm stock, quality CCB030. Same rules as ROUND20.

Both programs were imported on the emulated control on 24 Nov 2026 (`agie-imports-20261125/ROUND20` and `THREEARC`): zero steps at import, the 20 mm TECCUT row, `CCB030[4]` after TECCUT, `geen fouten`, every arc centre kept on every pass, 1.000 mm separation. The files are byte-identical at this head.
